Feature: From courts to lifestyles, tennis booms across China
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
09:34:30 CST
10:34:30 KST

by Sportswriters Li Chunyu, Li Bowen
BEIJING, Oct. 29 (Xinhua) -- As 16-year-old home prodigy Sun Xinran clinched the women's singles title at the ITF World Tennis Tour Junior Finals in Chengdu on Sunday, Chinese tennis embraced another highlight this autumn besides the ATP and WTA tournaments in the China Swing.
Running through September to November, the China Swing covers cities including Beijing, Shanghai, Wuhan, Chengdu, Hangzhou, Ningbo, Guangzhou and Hong Kong. The 2025 edition drew nearly one million on-site spectators, generating about 250 million yuan (37.5 million U.S. dollars) in ticket revenue and driving over 2.4 billion dollars in related consumption, according to the Tennis Administration Center.
The Tennis Administration Center had already moved to sustain that momentum, issuing reform measures in 2025 covering event supply, talent development and public participation. This September, ahead of the National Day holiday, the General Office of the State Council issued guidelines on unleashing the potential of sports consumption, explicitly supporting high-level professional events such as tennis.
The policy push and the season's momentum have met this autumn. The China Swing has become a window into China's tennis industry and sports-event consumption: from "second-screen" viewing areas to ticket-stub economies, from wild cards tilted toward young Chinese players to a public picking up rackets.
BREAKTHROUGHS AT HOME
Zheng Qinwen's triumph at the China Open was one of the most remarkable moments. The Olympic champion claimed her maiden WTA 1000 title to become the first Chinese player to win the tournament's women's singles crown.
"To play in China is like the fifth Grand Slam for me. I want to perform super well in front of my people," said Zheng, who celebrated her 24th birthday during the China Open in Beijing. "Coming back from the elbow injury, I find my inner fire back and want to be a more aggressive player."
Zheng was not the only Chinese player to benefit from home tournaments. Wild card Sun reached the women's singles last 32 at the China Open, where she faced opponents of rising rank with each round.
"This tournament gave me opportunity to play against top players. From the first round to the third round, my opponents are getting higher in their rankings. This really motivates me to improve myself," said Sun, who took the girls' singles title at this year's US Open.
At the Wuhan Open, qualifier Shi Han upset Alexandra Eala of the Philippines for her first WTA 1000 main-draw win.
Bai Xilin, director of China's Tennis Administration Center, noted that the China Swing provides more opportunities for home players with wild cards and qualifying matches.
"It serves to unleash the potential of our domestic players and inspire their growth in a long run through high-level events," Bai said.
For overseas athletes, the China Swing offers a chance to explore the host cities. Novak Djokovic took the Summer Palace as a favorite destination.
"I respect Chinese culture and tradition very much. Actually I was staying in a hotel that is just next to the Summer Palace. I've been going there every day. No joke. It's a stunning place more than just nature," said the 39-year-old Djokovic, who claimed his seventh China Open men's singles title this year.
"Tennis brings together players and fans from different countries and backgrounds. Through the tournament coverage and the players' own social channels, international audiences can also discover more aspects of China," said Fabrice Chouquet, a WTA senior official.
ECONOMIC ACES
For Vietnamese businessman Dang Phu, his destination in China has always been the Canton Fair in autumn. But this year, he and colleagues arrived earlier than usual to watch the Wuhan Open and then the Shanghai Masters.
"We wanted to see top players compete in person and experience the atmosphere," Dang said.
"People came to watch the match not only for the competition itself, but to feel the urban life. So, the organizers need to focus more on how an event can draw larger crowds and channel these visitors into a full range of consumption scenarios across the host city," said Huang Haiyan, a professor at Beijing Sport University.
According to the China Open organizing committee, total consumption during the tournament is projected to exceed 8.2 million dollars, up 55 percent year-on-year, with licensed product revenue doubling to 4.2 million dollars. Over 450,000 visitors entered the National Tennis Center, up 25 percent, including around 60 percent from other cities and nearly 10,000 international spectators.
Even though the Wuhan Open was not scheduled for the National Day holiday this year and home favorite Zheng was absent through injury, the tournament still drew 202,700 on-site spectators, 48 percent of whom traveled from other cities.
"The tournament not only drives direct spending on tickets, licensed products and catering services, but also spurs consumption on accommodation, transport and tourism," said Hong Xuyan, deputy director of the Wuhan Sports Bureau.
At the Shanghai Masters, around 248,000 on-site spectators watched the tournament, two thirds from outside Shanghai. "The total revenue reached 75 million dollars, with sponsorship contributing roughly 50 percent and ticketing for 20 percent," said Yang Yibin, chairman of Shanghai Juss Sports Development Group.
"Tennis fans feature high per-capita spending. They stay longer and always follow a complete consumption chain spanning tickets, catering, accommodation and tourism for multiplier effect," noted Wang Xueli, a professor at Tsinghua University's School of Economics and Management.
The broader industry is growing too. China's tennis industry was worth 5.5 billion dollars in 2024, up 15 percent year-on-year, according to the Tennis Administration Center.
NURTURING TENNIS CULTURE
Chinese tennis player Ji Mianyi, 20, sensed the tennis boom through her family and friends.
"When the topic turns to sports, they used to think of table tennis or badminton first. But after Zheng won the women's singles gold at the Paris 2024 Olympic Games, more people around me wanted to learn from scratch and asked me how long it takes to be able to compete," Ji said.
Her observations are borne out by the data. China's tennis population reached 25.19 million in 2024, up 28.03 percent from 19.67 million in 2021 and about a quarter of the global total, according to the Tennis Administration Center. The number of courts rose from 49,767 to 53,805 over the same period, up 8.12 percent.
Two decades ago, when Zheng Jie and Yan Zi claimed China's first women's doubles Grand Slam title at the 2006 Australian Open, tennis still seemed far from most Chinese people. The country had nearly two million participants and about 10,000 courts, according to figures from that year.
"There were much fewer youth tennis tournaments in China at that time," Zheng Jie recalled. "Then, the outstanding performance of Chinese players, including Li Na and Zheng Qinwen, kept stoking public enthusiasm for tennis."
By 2025, Guangdong, Sichuan, Hubei, Beijing and Zhejiang are the top five regions by tennis population, all hosting ATP or WTA tournaments as part of the China Swing. Only 5,402 youth players are registered with the General Administration of Sport, but roughly 506,000 young players have competition records outside the registered system, according to the Tennis Administration Center.
Shanghai, home to the Masters, has maintained strong momentum. At the PMAX Tennis Center, its 12 courts have become a thriving hub.
"Our tennis center hosts training courses and tournaments, catering to enthusiasts of different stages," introduced Jia Jingzhe, one of the center's partners. "Powered by this model, the center's monthly revenue has been around 200,000 dollars since March this year, more than quadrupling over four years compared with 2022."
Among the customers at PMAX, adults account for more than 60 percent, with women in the majority. According to the Shanghai Tennis Association, the city's tennis-playing population reached 980,000 in 2025, and more than 30 newly opened venues added over 100 standard courts.
"Tennis is an integral part of my life," said enthusiast Zhu Lingjun, who plays three to four hours every week and uses AI to review her game.
From professional tournaments to grassroots courts, tennis has been evolving into a lifestyle in China.
"International studies have found that long-term tennis participation can help extend people's lifespan by improving sleep and modulating nervous system," Bai said. "Our goal is to ensure that tennis is accessible to everyone, and we are striving toward that vision." ■

====================================================================================================

5 Things to Consider When Planning Interior Thresholds
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
01:30:00 UTC
10:30:00 KST

An opening between two rooms shapes how people move through a building, what they see from one space to another, and whether an area feels connected or separate. Although doors are among the most frequently used interior architectural elements, their impact on the interior organization is often considered late in the design process. Yet their movement and relationship to surrounding surfaces influence circulation, furniture placement, and the perception of space.
In residential renovations, these decisions are particularly important. Existing walls, structural elements, building services, and ceiling heights can limit options, while new layouts often balance open-plan living with the need for privacy. In new construction, architects have greater freedom to coordinate wall cavities, suspended ceilings, and door mechanisms from the outset.
The question is how two spaces should relate: remain connected, be separated, or alternate between the two? Openings, partitions, hinged doors, pivot doors, sliding doors, and furniture each offer different possibilities. Door systems such as those developed by ECLISSE provide different approaches to these transitions, responding to existing construction conditions and the intended spatial arrangement.
1. Defining the Relationship Between Spaces
A kitchen connected to a living room may benefit from a wide opening that preserves visual continuity while still allowing separation during cooking or entertaining. A home office may stay open during the day but still need visual and acoustic privacy for focused work or calls. In both cases, the design must balance openness with the option of separation.
Not every transition requires a door. Changes in floor finish, deeper openings, screens, or variations in ceiling height can distinguish areas without closing them off. Furniture can serve a similar purpose: a kitchen island, freestanding storage unit, or shelving system can define zones, guide circulation, and provide storage without creating a full-height partition.
2. Choosing a Door System
The door mechanism affects circulation and usable space. Hinged doors require clearance for their swing, which must be coordinated with furniture, corridors, and adjacent doors. Pivot doors let larger panels rotate around pivot points set away from a conventional side hinge.
Sliding doors move parallel to a wall or partition, avoiding the floor space a swinging panel requires. Ceiling-, surface-mounted, and integrated sliding door systems such as the ECLISSE Exo and Endo leave the panel visible when open, while pocket doors slide into a cavity within the wall. The latter leave the opening unobstructed and free up the adjacent wall surface, but require sufficient space within the partition and coordination with electrical installations and other services.
The distinction becomes particularly relevant in renovations. A ceiling- or surface-mounted track can be installed without creating a door cavity within the wall or requiring a suspended ceiling, which can simplify projects where existing construction must remain in place. A ceiling-integrated sliding door and pocket door may be easier to accommodate in a new partition designed around the mechanism. The decision depends on available construction depth, the intended opening, and the functions the surrounding wall must support.
3. Visible or Concealed
For sliding doors, the sliding mechanism is part of the architectural detail. Its position affects the ceiling, wall finish, and the opening's appearance when the panel is open or closed. Choosing between a visible track and a recessed system also influences how the door relates to surrounding surfaces.
In a ceiling- or surface-mounted sliding door system, such as the ECLISSE Exo, a track support is mounted on the wall or ceiling and concealed behind a 65-mm-high aluminum pelmet. Its appearance can coordinate with the surrounding surfaces or remain a visible architectural detail, available in finishes such as white, black, or a paintable primer.
A ceiling-integrated sliding door system, such as ECLISSE Endo, integrates the track support into a suspended ceiling. Once finished, the support sits flush with the ceiling, leaving only a slim slot for the visible sliding guide. The primer-coated surface can be painted to match the ceiling, allowing the mechanism to recede visually. The system can be installed in front of or inside the passageway, ideal for large openings. This approach requires the ceiling construction to accommodate the recessed support; however, it is adjustable and can accommodate unevenness in the ceiling slab. Both systems accommodate wooden panels and glass panels with aluminum frames. Individual panels can measure up to 1,300 mm wide and 3 m high, with a specified thickness of 40 mm.
4. Configuring Openings
The passage width affects the number of panels and the space needed for their movement. A single panel may suit a standard doorway, while wider openings can use two opposing panels that meet in the center. Multiple tracks accommodate several panels, and fixed panels can extend the overall glazed or opaque surface.
Sliding door systems, such as ECLISSE Exo and Endo, are available in single-, double-, and triple-track configurations. Both also allow two opposing panels on the same track, with fixed panels as an additional option. These arrangements can accommodate wider connections between living areas, kitchens, and multipurpose rooms. The open position requires as much consideration as the closed one. Available wall or ceiling length, where panels collect, and the position of switches and furniture all affect how much of the passage remains clear.
5. The Door as Part of the Interior
Material choices also affect the relationship between spaces. A door's finish influences how the threshold reads within a room. A panel matching the wall color can reduce visual interruptions, while contrasting timber, glass, or a dark track can emphasize the opening. Glass maintains visual continuity, while an opaque panel provides greater visual separation. A sliding panel can close off an area when needed and leave the layout open when retracted. Flush-to-wall doors offer another way to maintain continuity by aligning the door leaf with the surrounding wall.
The aim is not to make every boundary disappear, but to determine where it should remain visible, where it should recede, and how it should respond to everyday use. Coordinating the opening, panel movement, supporting structure, and finish allows doors to become part of the spatial plan.

Website reporting on crime in Victoria staffed by workers in Philippines
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
01:16:44 UTC
10:16:44 KST

News website reporting on crime in Victoria staffed by workers in Philippines
In short:
The director of a home security business has admitted to paying people in the Philippines to create stories about crime in Victoria for a news website he owns.
The stories on Victoria Crime News are credited to a fictional team of local Australian reporters.
The website has been recommended by AI chatbots as a reliable source of news despite some articles containing glaring errors.
The director of a website that reports news stories on Victorian crime has admitted its local team of reporters does not exist and that he uses workers in the Philippines.
Victoria Crime News (VCN) credits its stories to a four-person team of specialist crime reporters who have filed over 250 articles since February 2026.
But when ABC NEWS Verify spoke to its owner, Craig Winder, he admitted his team was not local at all.
"I have a team of writers over in the Philippines … I just tell them to not write anything incriminating."
The site features stories containing glaring errors and AI-generated photos.
Tests conducted by ABC NEWS Verify of prominent chatbots have found it is being recommended as a reliable source of information by Google's Gemini and X's Grok.
'Pink slime' journalism
The site is an example of so-called "pink slime" journalism, according to Momoko Fujita, a senior lecturer at the University of Canberra, who researches how digital platforms and media influence people's behaviour.
Pink slime refers to websites that purport to publish legitimate news but instead publish AI-enhanced content for the purpose of influencing audiences or generating revenue.
"If it's not fake, then why would they put fake names?" she said.
VCN claims its "editorial team may use generative-AI tools as part of research, headline drafting or copy editing", but assures readers that every article is written by a "named human reporter".
Over the phone, Mr Winder provided more detail on the VCN's human reporters, saying he actually employed a roster of workers based in the Philippines who filed stories attributed to fictitious reporters with "Aussie names" listed on the website's editorial team.
Mr Winder said he had "changed a lot of staff over the last three years" owing to resignations or poor performance.
When pressed by ABC NEWS Verify whether it was deceptive to use fake bios for his Philippines journalists, he said: "I suppose it is a bit deceptive, to be honest, just to be black and white."
Mr Winder told ABC NEWS Verify he set up the website to raise awareness of crime in his state and compel the government to "do more" to combat crime.
He is also the director of a company specialising in home security installations.
Mr Winder said he has been a victim of several attempted burglaries which partly motivated him to create a news website focusing on reporting crime in his state.
AI images and false details
Some of the news stories are factually incorrect or show indications of being AI-enhanced rewrites of stories first published by news outlets such as The Age and ABC News.
This includes the use of near-identical passages and VCN's inclusion of AI-generated images for some stories.
Some AI-generated images accompanying stories show little resemblance to the locations they purport to show.
A VCN image accompanying a story on the firebombing of a grocer in Melbourne's Deer Park, for instance, shows little resemblance to the actual shopfront, which was photographed following the blaze as part of the ABC's reporting.
A handful of stories are also accompanied by images that appear to have no relevance whatsoever.
The image used in this article bears no relationship to its subject. (Supplied: Victoria Crime News)
Other stories contain glaring factual errors.
VCN's story on the cold case homicide of Kade Hall claims Mr Hall was "last seen in 2014".
Details openly available on the Victoria Police website state that Mr Hall was last seen in 2002 when his body, which had sustained fatal gunshot wounds, was found in bushland near Kalorama in Victoria.
Other cold cases featured on the VCN website contain significant factual errors, such as the murder of Shannon McCormack, a man who was fatally assaulted in Melbourne's CBD in 2002 by an unknown assailant.
His case on the VCN website describes him as a female who was last seen in the early 2000s before mysteriously disappearing.
Mr Winder said he was surprised to learn about inaccuracies in articles on his website, telling ABC NEWS Verify that he would raise it with his team in the Philippines and correct any inaccuracies.
He said it was not his intention for the website to plagiarise original reporting by real reporters.
"I never want to take away from proper, true journalism and journalists, and I never want to take their information research away from them," he said.
Former police domain used for pink slime
The site's domain address was previously operated by the Victorian Police Force, which used it to publish official police announcements until 2019.
How the domain looked when it was run by Victoria Police in 2019. (Supplied: Victoria Police)
It was later acquired by Mr Winder, who used the domain to launch VCN, which started publishing stories in February 2026.
Dr Fujita agreed it was concerning the site was being recommended by AI chatbots, but she was unsurprised.
"[The chatbots] recommended this as a reliable source because … search engines use AI today.
"The way this website is structured, and the kind of keywords they use, is optimised for AI search engines."
She added the website's selective editorial focus "suggests there is [a] certain agenda behind this operation".

What is celebrated on October 29 in Ukraine and around the world
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
03:14:48 EET
10:14:48 KST

What is celebrated on October 29 in Ukraine and around the world
Kyiv • UNN
October 29 marks World Stroke Day, World Psoriasis Day, Financial Independence Day, and World Ultrasound Day. The faithful honor Anastasia of Rome.
On October 29, the world observes World Stroke Day and World Psoriasis Day under the auspices of international medical organizations. According to the new-style church calendar, Saint Anastasia the Roman, a venerable martyr, is commemorated, while according to the old style, Saint Longinus the Centurion, who stood by the Lord’s Cross, is remembered, UNN reports.
World Stroke Day
The date was established by the World Stroke Organization in 2006. The event is intended to draw public attention to cerebrovascular diseases, which are among the leading causes of disability and death worldwide. The day emphasizes the importance of prevention (controlling blood pressure, quitting smoking, and eating a healthy diet) and raising public awareness of the first symptoms of stroke using the BRAIN/FAST acronym, when timely assistance within the “golden window” of 4.5 hours can minimize severe consequences for the brain.
World Psoriasis Day
Established in 2004 at the initiative of the International Federation of Psoriasis Associations and officially supported by the World Health Organization. The medical observance aims to raise awareness of psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis—chronic autoimmune diseases affecting more than 125 million people worldwide. The event calls for overcoming the stigmatization and social isolation of patients, expanding access to modern biological medicines, and providing comprehensive psychological and dermatological care.
International Financial Independence Day
A popular international observance dedicated to promoting financial literacy, personal budget planning, and investment culture. The observance encourages people to build financial safety nets, optimize debt obligations, develop passive sources of income, and achieve personal material freedom from daily economic instability.
World Ultrasound Day
A professional and scientific observance for ultrasound diagnostics specialists, recognizing the revolutionary contribution of ultrasound technologies to medicine, industry, and scientific research. In healthcare, ultrasound is one of the safest, most accessible, and most highly informative methods for imaging organs, blood vessels, and fetal development during pregnancy.
According to the new calendar, Orthodox and Greek Catholic believers commemorate Saint Anastasia the Roman, a venerable martyr—a Christian maiden who was raised in a monastery near Rome. During the persecution under Emperor Decius, she openly professed her faith in Christ before the governor Probus, endured brutal torture, and accepted a martyr’s death by beheading.
According to the old calendar, believers commemorate Saint Longinus the Centurion —a Roman centurion who stood guard by the Lord’s Cross on Golgotha and witnessed the crucifixion and subsequent Resurrection of Christ. Having seen the miracles, Longinus believed in the Savior, refused the bribe offered by the Jewish elders, left military service, and set out to preach the Gospel in his homeland of Cappadocia, where he was later executed on the orders of Pontius Pilate.

Scientists discover a hidden oxygen reservoir deep inside Earth
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
01:13:05 UTC
10:13:05 KST

Scientists discover a hidden oxygen reservoir deep inside Earth
- Date:
- October 28, 2026
- Source:
- Science China Press
- Summary:
- Scientists have discovered that magma deep inside Earth can store surprising amounts of extra oxygen, potentially revealing a hidden contributor to our planet's oxygen-rich atmosphere. The findings suggest that ancient volcanic eruptions may have helped transform Earth's atmosphere billions of years ago, with implications for understanding life on other planets.
- Share:
Scientists have discovered that molten rock deep inside Earth can store far more oxygen than previously believed. The finding challenges long-standing assumptions about magma and raises an intriguing possibility: oxygen released from Earth's interior may have helped transform the planet's atmosphere billions of years ago.
Through high-pressure experiments and advanced computer simulations, researchers found that magma can absorb additional oxygen beyond the amount normally required by its chemical composition. This hidden oxygen could provide a previously unrecognized connection between Earth's deep interior, volcanic activity, and the development of an oxygen-rich atmosphere.
The research was led by Dr. Yanhao Lin and Dr. Ho-kwang Mao of the Center for High Pressure Science and Technology Advanced Research (HPSTAR), working with Prof. Haiyang Niu of Northwestern Polytechnical University and Prof. Wim van Westrenen of Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam. Their findings were published in National Science Review.
Scientists Challenge a Long-Standing Assumption About Magma
Oxygen is one of the most abundant elements inside Earth, accounting for more than half of the atoms in the planet's silicate interior. Silicates are minerals and molten materials composed primarily of silicon and oxygen, along with other elements. They make up much of Earth's mantle and crust.
Despite oxygen's abundance, scientists have traditionally assumed that magma can contain only a specific amount of it. Under this understanding, the oxygen content is determined by the quantities and electrical charge states of other elements in the molten rock, including silicon, magnesium, and iron.
Water and carbon dioxide behave differently. Both can dissolve in magma and later escape as gases when the surrounding pressure decreases. These substances are known as volatile components, and their release plays an important role in volcanic activity.
Oxygen, however, has generally not been treated as a separate volatile substance that magma can absorb and release. Whether molten silicate rock could hold additional oxygen independently of its ordinary chemical composition remained largely unexplored.
The new research suggests that this assumption may need to change.
Extreme Pressure Reveals Hidden Oxygen in Molten Rock
To investigate, the scientists recreated conditions found deep within Earth using laboratory equipment capable of generating extraordinary pressures and temperatures.
They heated a synthetic version of mid-ocean ridge basalt, a type of volcanic rock commonly produced where tectonic plates move apart beneath the oceans. The samples were exposed to pressures ranging from normal atmospheric pressure to 7 gigapascals and temperatures between 1200 and 1800 °C.
A pressure of 7 gigapascals is approximately 69,000 times the atmospheric pressure at Earth's surface.
The team used specialized piston-cylinder and cubic presses to maintain these extreme conditions. They also added platinum oxide (PtO2) to establish an oxygen-rich environment and test how much additional oxygen the molten rock could absorb.
After the experiments, the researchers rapidly cooled the molten material, producing glass that preserved important characteristics of the melt. They then analyzed its elemental composition and measured the amounts of water and carbon dioxide present.
By calculating how much oxygen was needed to balance the other elements, along with the oxygen already contained in water and carbon dioxide, the scientists could estimate how much remained unaccounted for.
They called this additional amount "excess oxygen."
The results revealed a striking relationship between pressure and oxygen storage.
At normal atmospheric pressure, the glass contained almost no excess oxygen. At 7 gigapascals, however, excess oxygen accounted for more than 5% of the sample's weight.
For comparison, experiments conducted at similar pressures and temperatures without added platinum oxide produced excess oxygen concentrations of only 0.2% to 0.5% by weight.
The researchers also wanted to determine whether the additional oxygen was truly incorporated into the material or merely trapped as tiny gas bubbles.
Using Raman spectroscopy, a technique that identifies substances by examining how they interact with light, they found no detectable signature of oxygen gas in the glass. This indicated that the excess oxygen had become part of the glass structure rather than accumulating in bubbles.
The measured concentrations may even underestimate magma's actual oxygen-storage capacity. Some oxygen could have escaped while the molten samples were cooling, meaning the original melts may have contained still greater amounts.
Computer Simulations Reveal How Magma Stores Extra Oxygen
To better understand the discovery at the atomic level, Prof. Niu led a series of theoretical computer simulations.
The researchers used deep neural network (DNN) models to simulate interactions among atoms with accuracy approaching that of ab initio calculations, which describe atomic behavior using fundamental principles of quantum mechanics.
The simulations showed that additional oxygen could dissolve into molten material until the system reached equilibrium, a state in which oxygen entering and leaving the melt is balanced.
Although the computer models used a simplified system containing only magnesium, silicon, and oxygen, they reproduced the same overall pattern observed in the laboratory: magma's ability to hold excess oxygen increased with pressure.
The simulated oxygen concentrations were lower than the experimental measurements, which the scientists attributed to differences between the simplified model and the more complex chemical composition of actual basalt.
The calculations also revealed changes in how oxygen atoms behaved as more oxygen entered the melt. Their electrical charges became more varied, and a small proportion formed peroxide-like bonds, in which oxygen atoms bond to one another.
These changes help explain how molten rock might accommodate oxygen beyond the amount predicted by conventional chemical models.
Importantly, the pressure-dependent behavior resembles that of water and carbon dioxide, which also become more soluble in magma as pressure increases.
Based on these findings, the researchers propose that oxygen should be recognized as an independent component of silicate melts, rather than being considered only in relation to other elements.
Could Ancient Volcanoes Have Helped Oxygenate Earth's Atmosphere?
The discovery raises a much larger question about Earth's history: Could magma have transported significant amounts of oxygen from the planet's interior to its surface?
The researchers suggest a possible mechanism involving magma generated in oxidized regions of Earth's mantle.
Under the immense pressures deep underground, this magma could absorb substantial quantities of excess oxygen. As it moves upward, the surrounding pressure decreases, reducing the amount of oxygen the molten rock can retain.
Some of that oxygen could then be released, potentially contributing to chemical reactions that increase the oxidation of the upper mantle, Earth's crust, and eventually the atmosphere.
Oxidation refers to chemical processes involving the transfer of electrons. In this context, oxygen carried by magma could increase the oxidizing capacity of surrounding materials and potentially influence the balance of oxygen in the atmosphere.
This proposed mechanism may also help explain an intriguing coincidence in Earth's geological past.
Between approximately 2.5 billion and 2.0 billion years ago, atmospheric oxygen levels underwent major increases. This interval overlaps with the formation of some of Earth's largest large igneous provinces (LIPs), enormous regions of volcanic rock created by exceptionally large outpourings of magma.
The researchers suggest that oxygen released from these ancient volcanic systems could have contributed to changes in atmospheric composition.
Their preliminary calculation highlights the potentially enormous scale of the process. They estimate that if magma erupted during this period released excess oxygen equal to just 0.27% of its weight, the total amount could theoretically match all the oxygen present in Earth's atmosphere today.
This does not establish that volcanic activity actually supplied that much atmospheric oxygen. Instead, it illustrates how even a relatively small release of oxygen from immense quantities of magma could have major planetary consequences.
A New Clue to Earth's Evolution and Habitable Planets
The findings could influence several important areas of planetary science.
For one, they may change how scientists understand ancient magma oceans, vast regions of molten rock believed to have existed during the early evolution of Earth and other rocky planets.
They also introduce a possible new factor in volcanic degassing, the process through which gases and other volatile substances escape from molten rock and interact with a planet's atmosphere.
If magma can store and release oxygen independently of its other chemical components, models of Earth's atmospheric development may need to account for this previously overlooked process.
The implications could extend beyond Earth. Understanding how oxygen moves between the interiors and atmospheres of rocky planets may help researchers investigate the conditions that allow potentially habitable environments to develop and persist over billions of years.
Although further research is needed to establish how much oxygen natural magmas carry and how much reaches the atmosphere, the discovery points to a surprising possibility: some of the processes that helped shape Earth's oxygen-rich environment may have originated far beneath the planet's surface.
Story Source:
Materials provided by Science China Press. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Yongjiang Xu, Haiyang Niu, Wim van Westrenen, Ruiheng Liu, Peiyan Wu, Ho-Kwang Mao, Yanhao Lin. Magma as a carrier of non-stoichiometric oxygen linking Earth’s interior and atmosphere. National Science Review, 2026; 13 (18) DOI: 10.1093/nsr/nwag539

A mysterious tomb more than 4,000 years old with two stone “antennas” has been found in the Sahara
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher

A mysterious tomb more than 4,000 years old with two stone “antennas” has been found in the Sahara
Kyiv • UNN
Archaeologists examined a 54.5-meter-long tomb with two stone protrusions. Inside, they found a skeleton and four beads.
Archaeologists investigated an unusual stone tomb in Western Sahara, built more than 4,000 years ago. The nearly 55-meter-long structure has two long stone projections resembling antennae, whose purpose remains a mystery. Science & Vie reports this, citing a study in the journal African Archaeological Review, writes UNN.
Details
The tomb is located near the Sluguilla-Lawash rock art site. It consists of an oval mound about 12 meters in diameter and two parallel rows of stone slabs directed eastward.
The structure is 54.5 meters long in total. Local limestone was used in its construction, and the stones were laid without mortar.
A skeleton and ostrich eggshell ornaments were found inside
Under the mound, archaeologists discovered the remains of one person approximately 25–35 years old. Because of the poor condition of the bones, it was impossible to determine the sex of the deceased.
Four ring-shaped beads made from ostrich eggshells were found near the skeleton. The researchers found no other burial goods.
To determine the age of the tomb, scientists from the University of Girona used radiocarbon analysis of the mineral component of the bones. The results showed that the burial is approximately 4,100–4,417 years old.
According to the researchers, this is the first direct dating of a burial of this type in the Atlantic Sahara region.
The scientists suggest that the structure was built during a period when the Sahara's climate was significantly wetter and the area was inhabited by ancient pastoralist and hunter communities.

This is especially important for the Philippines, which has the distinction of being both a U.S. treaty ally and a South China Sea claimant state that disputes China’s maximalist claims to the vital waterway. The past few years have seen growing tensions between Beijing and Manila in contested parts of the South China Sea, where the two sides have engaged in a string of dangerous confrontations.
In his own remarks to the ADMM, Philippine Defense Secretary Gilbert Teodoro Jr. said that ASEAN values the United States’ “sustained engagement” with the region’s defense establishments, pointing out that “a robust U.S. presence is necessary for peace and stability in Southeast Asia and in the broader Indo-Pacific region.”
Even then, the erratic nature of current U.S. foreign policy would likely be a source of consternation in most, if not all, ASEAN capitals. Southeast Asia has been hit hard by the effects of the U.S.-Israeli attack on Iran earlier this year, which exposed the heavy dependence of most nations on imported oil and refined fuels from the Gulf. The Trump administration’s erratic tariff policy – Southeast Asian nations were among the heaviest hit by Trump’s initial “liberation day” tariff announcement – has also impacted the region’s economies, and prompted some nations to begin diversifying their trade partnerships. On top of this, the U.S.’ staunch support for Israel, and its role in the Israeli assaults on Gaza, remains a subject of concern in Muslim-majority Southeast Asia.
Even in terms of security cooperation and military deployments, a traditional area of strength, the U.S. walks a fine line between supporting deterrence by bolstering Southeast Asian defense capacity and actions that ratchet up tensions with China. While the Trump administration has dialed down tensions with Beijing, its highly disruptive war on Iran, the accompanying rhetoric of which has hardly eschewed “needless escalation or public theatrics,” naturally raises the question of whether this U.S. administration, or a future Trump-ite administration, could bluster its way into some sort of conflict with China.
Greg Poling, director of the Asia Maritime Transparency Initiative at the Center for Strategic and International Studies in Washington, D.C., told Reuters that Hegseth would get an opportunity to discuss the above issues with ASEAN counterparts, although he expected that concrete cooperation would be concentrated among “like-minded” countries.

Australia has highest rates of anorexia and bulimia globally
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
01:00:22 UTC
10:00:22 KST

Australia has highest rates of anorexia and bulimia in world, study finds
In short:
Global cases of anorexia and bulimia nervosa have increased by 71 per cent since 1990.
Australia has the highest rates per 100,000 people for the two eating disorders in the world.
What's next?
Experts suggest more needs to be done, including increasing funding to ensure the numbers do not continue rising.
Cases of anorexia and bulimia nervosa are affecting Australians at a world-leading rate.
The unenviable record comes amid a 71 per cent increase in cases of the two eating disorders globally in the past 30 years.
This jump translates to about 18.1 million people worldwide living with anorexia or bulimia as of 2023, according to a study published today in JAMA Psychiatry.
Australia has the highest rate of any country in the world, with 1,026.5 per 100,000 people estimated to have one of the two disorders.
University of Queensland epidemiologist and study senior author Damian Santomauro said Australia's ranking was "surprising and concerning".
"Usually we do see higher prevalence of eating disorders in high-income settings," he said.
"[But] I'm surprised to see it as high as it actually is compared to the US or other locations in Western Europe."
Eating disorders disproportionately affect younger people and are a mental health condition involving an unhealthy relationship with food.
Butterfly Helpline clinical psychologist Sarah Cox said the study confirmed what people with lived experience of eating disorders, their families and healthcare professionals had been reporting for years.
"Eating disorders are serious mental illnesses that affect a significant number of people in Australia, and that the number of people affected is growing," Ms Cox said.
How data was calculated
The findings are part of the Global Burden of Disease study, the world's largest health project that includes research about the impact of mental disorders on the overall population.
"It was the first of its kind that really highlighted that mental disorders can be on par or if not more burdensome than some physical disorders," Dr Santomauro said.
To calculate the prevalence of these disorders, researchers use surveys rather than treatment data to ensure they capture people who may not have access to treatment.
This allows them to analyse data from around the world since 1990, when the study began.
Worldwide, the researchers estimated 3.92 million people had anorexia and 14.2 million had bulimia. They forecasted cases would keep growing through to 2050 globally.
They also calculated that for the two eating disorders, that led to a loss of 3.81 million disability adjusted life years around the world.
Dr Santomauro noted that Australia's high number of cases may be partially due to the way survey data was collected.
"Almost all the surveys that are done in Australia tend to use a different methodology [to the rest of the world]," he said.
"But I don't think that it's purely because of that type of data."
Ms Cox said the numbers, while high, might also mean Australia had more research and data.
"We might be seeing the problem more clearly than other countries," she said.
Impact higher for youth and females
Dr Santomauro was not surprised cases had increased globally, and said that although there were many factors, one "hypothesis" was increased time online.
"I would expect prevalence to get worse in more recent years because of social media, the Instagram and body image issues that youth are encountering today," he said.
Females accounted for nearly 70 per cent of the 18.1 million global cases and about 41 per cent of all global cases were in young people aged 10 to 24.
Jeanette Chan, an economist and public policy professional who has lived experience with an eating disorder, said people from migrant and non-western backgrounds could have more difficulty gaining help for eating disorders.
"Growing up as a migrant, I didn't have a lot of language or understanding around what mental health was or what mental health issues were," they said.
"In Australia, we're a very multicultural society, and eating disorders are often a very Western conceptualisation of issues surrounding food and eating.
"That affects the way that we make sense of what is problematic."
While Jeanette was able to gain help for her eating disorder, they said more funding for treatment and prevention was needed.
"There's been a lot more investment, but not enough in eating disorders in Australia over the last several years," they said.
Case numbers are underestimated in Australia and abroad
While Australia had the highest rates, the largest relative increases in the incidence of anorexia and bulimia occurred in East Asia, South Asia, and South-East Asia.
The study noted a few limitations, including data gaps for mortality related to bulimia, as well as less information from some low-income countries.
Dr Santomauro said the impact of eating disorders broadly was also underestimated since only anorexia and bulimia were included.
"The numbers … sound very, very large, but it's also really capturing a small proportion of the total eating disorder burden globally.
"There's also binge eating disorder, unspecified feeding or eating disorder and other very prevalent eating disorders that we don't capture."
Ms Cox agreed.
"In Australia, more than 1.1 million people will experience an eating disorder in any given year," she said.
"While anorexia and bulimia are serious eating disorders worthy of attention, we also need to expand the research focus to ensure people living with … other eating disorders are included in the conversation. "
Ms Cox said projections that cases would continue to rise highlighted the need to fund early treatment and prevention.
"We can lower these numbers, and there is more that can be done," she said.
"Getting help early improves the chances of recovery, but many people face barriers to care, including cost, living in regional areas and stigma, and many people with an eating disorder never get treatment."

What Quentin Tarantino’s Reservoir Dogs says about the US midterms
The tipping discussion in Tarantino’s 1992 crime thriller was unexpectedly prescient about American capitalism’s trajectory
3-MIN READ3-MIN
1
 Listen
Chow Chung-yan began his journalistic career at the South China Morning Post and rose to become editor-in-chief in 2025. 
When I first watched Quentin Tarantino’s Reservoir Dogs in 1992, I was struck by its inventive opening. Tarantino launched a gritty crime thriller not with a gunfight or a heist but with eight mobsters in a diner, finishing breakfast while bickering over Madonna and tipping etiquette.
By depicting hardened criminals as ordinary men carping about daily trivialities, Tarantino dispensed with the genre’s macho clichés, rendering the characters disarmingly authentic. Decades later, the subject of tipping still dominates daily American life.
On my recent visit to the United States, that famous anti-tipping monologue came back to me like recurring deja vu. Whether in conversation with intellectuals, corporate executives or hard-pressed students, the subject inevitably surfaced. Increasingly, I heard Mr Pink’s voice, the mobster who stubbornly refused to tip, echoed by people born long after the film’s release and by those who have never seen it.

COP31 must amplify people power, not oil lobby voices
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
01:00:00 UTC
10:00:00 KST

The climate crisis is also a human rights crisis – claiming lives and turning life upside down for countless communities across the world.
But while those profiting from fossil fuel expansion retain privileged access and influence over global climate negotiations, the people facing its harshest consequences, such as Indigenous Peoples or those living in climate-vulnerable communities, remain largely shut out of the decision-making.
As directors of Amnesty International in Brazil, Türkiye and Australia, countries with a leading role in COP30 and COP31, we have seen how effective climate action depends on people being able to speak, organise, protest and participate.
Last year in Belém, fossil fuel lobbyists outnumbered every national delegation except Brazil’s, exposing the imbalance of power within climate negotiations. COP31 should confront corporate capture and expand public participation. Instead, serious concerns have been raised over whether civil society will be able to speak freely and safely in Türkiye.
Rights curbs supercharge climate breakdown
Yet, the human rights needed to confront this crisis and demand justice are being eroded.
Authoritarian practices are supercharging climate breakdown by restricting protest, silencing defenders and shielding fossil fuel interests from scrutiny. Attacks on women, LGBTI+ people or members of other marginalised communities divide societies, weaken collective action and divert public attention while fossil fuel expansion continues.
That is why the assault on civic space in Türkiye, the host of COP31, should alarm every government preparing to attend the summit.
In September, Turkish authorities launched a nationwide operation targeting LGBTI+ organisations, activists and human rights defenders. Homes, venues and offices were raided, people were arrested and imprisoned, and social media accounts belonging to activists, journalists and human rights groups were restricted, including that of Amnesty International Türkiye.
This is part of a decade-long crackdown that has weakened judicial independence, ignored international judgments and restricted peaceful assembly, association and expression. Whoever is targeted, the effect is the same: dissent is silenced and fear spreads.
For COP31 to succeed, Türkiye must end its human rights crackdown.
“For COP31 to succeed, Türkiye must end its human rights crackdown. “
Worrying signals from co-host Türkiye
Against this backdrop, the agreement between Türkiye and the UN on hosting COP31 is alarming.
Article 11.11 requires participants to respect Türkiye’s laws and regulations and refrain from interfering in its “internal affairs”. Article 11.12 reintroduces language on waiving immunity that was omitted from Brazil’s COP30 agreement.
Turkish authorities are already invoking vague notions of “public morality” and “harm to the family” to investigate people and restrict expression. The agreement could therefore have a chilling effect on activists, defenders and journalists.
Could criticism of Türkiye’s fossil fuel policies, its treatment of environmental defenders or its crackdown on LGBTI+ organizations be characterised as interference in “internal affairs”? Nobody attending a UN climate conference should have to ask.
Türkiye and the UN should publicly guarantee that participants can speak, organise, report and protest peacefully without discrimination, intimidation, surveillance, detention or reprisals. Governments ought to challenge the agreement’s flaws before arriving in Antalya.
Brazil offered progress, but not perfection
COP31 must build on Brazil’s approach. Its COP hosting agreement committed to an inclusive and non-discriminatory conference, while its presidency adopted a more open and participatory tone. COP30 saw record participation by Indigenous Peoples, but access did not guarantee influence: many key decisions continued to be shaped behind closed doors.
Commitments made in Belém ultimately depend on domestic political choices, and Brazil’s October election results point to a legislature that may be less willing to uphold them. This could put the rights of Indigenous Peoples, Quilombola and traditional communities at greater risk.
When protections at home weaken, international spaces become even more vital for affected populations to speak out, and hold decision-makers accountable. COP31 must guarantee freedom of expression and peaceful assembly outside the “Blue Zone” (the UN-protected area) and grant civil society greater access to negotiations.
Environmental defenders are driving change
As documented by Amnesty International, communities resisting fossil fuel expansion and building fairer alternatives are facing harassment, surveillance, criminalization, disinformation, violence and restrictions on peaceful protest. They include: First Nations people in Australia challenging offshore oil and gas exploration, artisanal fishers in Brazil’s Guanabara Bay fighting for environmental justice, and activists defending Akbelen Forest in Türkiye from coal mining expansion.
These communities are rights-holders, knowledge-bearers, and political actors protecting territories and forging effective climate responses. Governments must protect them and ensure they have a meaningful say.
Discover more stories of environmental human rights defenders around the world who are standing up for people and the planet:
COP31 must confront fossil fuel power
To protect human rights, governments must use COP31 to advance three urgent priorities.
First, they must end fossil fuel expansion and accelerate a full, fast, fair, funded and human rights-compliant transition away from fossil fuels. States most responsible must go further and faster, ending fossil fuel subsidies and redirecting public resources towards rights-respecting renewable energy.
Second, they must ensure the transition protects rights and leaves no one behind, including by making the Just Transition Mechanism operational, funded and accountable.
And third, they must scale up public, grants-based climate finance for mitigation, adaptation and loss and damage, without pushing lower-income countries further into debt.
COP31 will not deliver these outcomes without the knowledge and expertise of front-line communities.
Brazil must defend the participatory progress made at COP30. Türkiye must reverse its crackdown and protect civic space. Australia, as president of negotiations, should secure an ambitious, human rights-centred outcome while confronting restrictions on peaceful climate protest at home.
The climate crisis cannot be solved behind closed doors. The doors must remain open, and people must have the power to shape what happens inside.
“The climate crisis cannot be solved behind closed doors. The doors must remain open, and people must have the power to shape what happens inside.”

- The move protects US manufacturers for now, but tariffs may still come if talks fail; the FCC also barred new Chinese robots and power inverters.
AI generated
WASHINGTON – US President Donald Trump found on Oct 28 that imported robotics and machinery pose national security risks but did not impose any immediate tariffs, instead ordering officials to hold talks with foreign governments on import levels.
The decision spares US manufacturers, which rely on foreign imports for most types of robotics and industrial machinery, from immediate new tariffs but leaves open the threat of tariffs if talks with trading partners fall short.
Following a probe that lasted more than a year, Trump directed the US Commerce Department and US Trade Representative to jointly negotiate agreements with trading partners to address concerns about imported robotics and industrial machinery, and said he could still impose tariffs at a later date.
He directed the agencies to report back in 180 days on the status of the talks with trading partners.
Trump in September 2025 opened a probe to review imported robotics and industrial machinery, such as programmable computer-controlled mechanical systems and industrial stamping and pressing machines.
The robotics probe covered machine tools for cutting, welding and handling workpieces, autoclaves and industrial ovens.
Laser and water-cutting tools and machinery are also included.
The US Federal Communications Commission in July barred imports of new models of Chinese robots and power inverters.
The rule allows existing models of humanoid and quadruped robots to be imported.
Some analysts forecast broad adoption of humanoid robots, topped with AI-enabled “brains”, in consumer and industrial arenas, while booming data centre construction in the US will depend on reliable sources of inverters.
“(Robots) collect data that could be leveraged by malign actors to surveil Americans, enhance the capabilities of foreign intelligence services, or to remotely commandeer the robots,” the FCC said in July.
The Commerce Department said the United States relies on foreign imports for most types of robotics and industrial machinery.
In July, the department completed a probe into imported commercial aircraft, jet engines and parts, and found foreign goods raise US national security concerns. REUTERS

Canada and EU drop associate membership plan in bid to deepen ties
Canada and the European Union will pursue closer ties but have dropped a proposal for associate EU membership, according to a joint declaration ahead of Thursday’s summit in Montreal. Prime Minister Mark Carney is seeking to reduce Canada’s reliance on the US, despite warnings from Donald Trump.
Canada and the European Union (EU) agreed to "ever closer association" but dropped the contentious idea of associate EU membership in a joint declaration seen by Reuters ahead of a Montreal summit hosted by Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney starting on Thursday.
The declaration, which officials plan to make public on Friday, said work to define the Canada-EU relationship would continue until another summit next year.
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen's suggestion of associate membership six weeks ago had been a divisive issue in negotiations among EU countries on the summit declaration, with Germany leading a group that argued they could not sign up to a concept that had no legal status and had not been fleshed out, diplomats said.
Deeper ties to Europe are an important part of Carney's strategy to reduce Canada’s economic and security reliance on America since US President Donald Trump imposed tariffs on Canadian goods. Still, Canada's efforts to draw closer to the EU risk angering Trump as trade talks between Canada and the US continue.
There is no precedent or legal definition for an EU “associate member”.

Trump previously called the EU’s proposal to make Canada an associate member “laughable” and said if he interpreted the move as a “hostile act,” the US might stop trading with Europe “on many things”.
Carney told reporters on Tuesday that the summit this week is the launch of further formal negotiations that will take another year.
“The good news is it doesn’t matter about specific names or nomenclature,” Carney said. “What matters is the difference it will make to the lives of Canadians.”
A previous draft statement had included at least two references to Canada as an associate member, including an acknowledgement that defining the term would take another year.
The statement includes a joint initiative to improve international connectivity between Europe, Canada and Asia through "new subsea cable infrastructure". 'Highly provocative' statement

Screwworm infests dog in Arizona, widening US cases

Screwworm infests dog in Arizona, widening US cases
- New World screwworm has infested a dog in Arizona, the third US state affected. The dog had a wound with maggots, and testing confirmed the case.
- The USDA is restricting animal movement near the area, stepping up checks, and releasing sterile flies. State vet Dr Ryan Wolker said: “We have been preparing for this possibility for a long while and are acting swiftly.”
- The outbreak is spreading again after decades of eradication, with 71 US cases since June and 18 active. It is also complicating livestock trade with Mexico and adding pressure to record beef prices.
AI generated
WASHINGTON – New World screwworm, a parasitic fly that eats warm-blooded animals alive, has infested a dog in Arizona, widening cases to a third US state, the US Department of Agriculture said on Oct 28.
The first detection in Arizona was in Cochise County, which borders Mexico, according to the USDA.
The dog had a wound on its back that was infested with maggots, consistent with screwworm, and scientific testing verified the infestation, the Arizona Department of Agriculture said.
The dog was receiving veterinary care, it added.
“We have been preparing for this possibility for a long while and are acting swiftly,” state veterinarian Dr Ryan Wolker said in a statement.
The Arizona case marks the latest sign that screwworm, eradicated from the US decades ago, may be regaining a foothold despite federal efforts to contain it, complicating the USDA’s attempts to reopen livestock trade with Mexico and ease record beef prices ahead of the mid-term elections.
The USDA said it was restricting animal movement in a 20km zone around the case, increasing surveillance of live animals and releasing sterile flies that combat screwworm in response to the infestation.
The agency halted livestock imports from Mexico in 2025 to try to keep out screwworm, which advanced north through Mexico and Latin America.
It detected screwworm in a calf in Texas in June and then confirmed additional cases in Texas and New Mexico.
As of Oct 28, the agency had reported 71 screwworm cases since June, and 18 were active, according to its website.
Infestations have multiplied since September, when there were only two active cases.
The import halt helped tighten US cattle supplies and push beef prices to record highs for American consumers, raising concerns about affordability ahead of the midterm elections.
The USDA began to resume livestock imports from Mexico in August and has restarted trade at three ports of entry in Arizona and New Mexico.
The agency has said it next plans to resume imports from Mexico in Nogales, Arizona, on Nov 30, if conditions for safe trade are in place.
Last week, the USDA confirmed the first case of screwworm in US wildlife in an elk in Texas. REUTERS

Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre
BENGALURU: Space regulator-cum-promoter Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN-SPACe) has selected six private space-sector entities for seed-fund grants under its AI INSPIRED programme, which aims to encourage the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in space technology.The projects span precision landing, space situational awareness, debris detection, satellite servicing and refuelling, automated target recognition, and spacecraft autonomy. Two other entities have been selected for mentorship and technical support, including access to Isro facilities for technology validation.The programme, announced in Feb 2026 under IN-SPACe’s Seed Fund Scheme, has a total outlay of up to Rs 6 crore, with each selected entity eligible for a grant of up to Rs 1 crore. The funding is intended to help start-ups and micro and small enterprises develop AI-based solutions for space applications.Among the selected projects, Agnikul Cosmos will develop an edge AI-enabled vision-based terminal navigation module for precision landing. The technology is aimed at improving navigation during the final stages of a landing manoeuvre.Digantara has been selected for its Agentic RSO Evaluation Suite (ARES), while EON Space Labs will develop an intelligent optical payload using field-programmable gate array (FPGA)-based edge AI.
The latter project aims to enable real-time space situational awareness and detection of space debris.OrbitAid Aerospace will work on machine-learning-assisted pose estimation algorithms for on-orbit servicing and refuelling. Such algorithms can help spacecraft determine their relative positions and orientations, an important requirement for operations involving approaching, docking with or servicing another spacecraft.Omnipresent Robot Technologies has been selected for an automated target recognition project covering applications such as defence and docking. TakeMeToSpace will work on adaptive spacecraft autonomy through an AI modernisation programme for attitude determination and control systems (ADCS), which help establish a spacecraft's orientation and maintain its intended direction.
IN-SPACe has also selected Foucault Private Limited and AkashaVeda Technologies for mentorship and technical support, although they are not listed among the six seed-fund grantees.
Foucault will work on an autonomous collision avoidance system for spacecraft using AI and machine learning. AkashaVeda’s project focuses on AI-based mission management, covering both onboard and ground operations. The two entities will receive opportunities to use IN-SPACe and Isro facilities to validate their technologies. They will also be considered for technology transfer from the Department of Space.As per IN-SPACe, the initiative is part of its efforts to expand private participation in India’s space sector by supporting the development of indigenous technologies and products.

US Justice Department loses initial bid to block votes from alleged non-citizens in California

- Judge David Carter said the request broke constitutional rules and warned it could cause chaos, erode trust, and wrongly strip voters of their rights.
- The Justice Department appealed, while California said its safeguards are strong and the federal claims rely on “suspect data”; similar moves were also made in Alaska and Washington.
AI generated
LOS ANGELES – A US judge strongly rebuked the Trump administration on Oct 28 by rejecting a request by the Justice Department to temporarily block California from counting any mail ballots for the midterm elections from more than 20,000 registered voters the department alleges are likely non-citizens.
The decision marks the latest setback for President Donald Trump’s effort to boost the federal government’s role in elections ahead of the Nov 3 midterms, with his Republican Party locked in a tight battle to retain control of both houses of Congress.
US District Judge David Carter issued the decision after a hearing on Oct 27 in Los Angeles federal court over the Justice Department’s request for a temporary restraining order barring officials from counting any ballots from the individuals it flagged.
The Justice Department’s lawsuit, filed on Oct 15, was a rare intervention in the voting process weeks before an election and signalled the Trump administration’s willingness to contest the midterm results in court.
“Never before in American history has the federal government, on the eve of an election, sought to coerce a state and local government to abandon its own constitutional election procedures and bend to the will of the executive branch,” Carter wrote on Oct 28.
The judge, an appointee of then Democratic President Bill Clinton, said the Justice Department’s last-minute request to exclude more than 20,000 ballots ran afoul of “longstanding constitutional principles mandating that states have control over their elections”.
Carter warned that a ruling in the Trump administration’s favour could create chaos and cause thousands of registered voters to “potentially lose the right that generations of Americans have fought to preserve”.
“Eroded trust in our democracy is irreparable,” Carter wrote. “Once a vote is segregated, lasting harm has occurred. If the executive (branch) can discount votes and threaten an ongoing election due to unproven allegations, then our democracy is in danger.”
The Justice Department swiftly appealed the decision to the 9th US Circuit Court of Appeals.
“Every day, more ballots are processed by election officials,” Justice Department lawyer Bill Essayli said in a statement.
“This ongoing emergency disenfranchises American citizens through dilution.”
California has said the state’s safeguards against non-citizen voting are robust. It said the Justice Department’s assertions relied on “suspect data” and that complying with its demands would risk disenfranchising eligible voters.
California is the most populous US state and a Democratic stronghold. It has more seats in the House of Representatives – 52 – than any other state.
Trump has made California a focal point of his sweeping immigration crackdown since returning to the White House, accusing it of undermining public safety through its “sanctuary state” policies that limit cooperation with federal immigration enforcement.
Trump has repeatedly insisted that states are not doing enough to stop voting by non-citizens, which he says is widespread despite multiple studies and state audits showing it is rare.
Appeals court rejected emergency request
The hearing comes after a federal appeals court on Oct 26 rejected an unusual emergency request by the Justice Department asking the appeals court to temporarily block California from counting the ballots before Carter had the chance to rule.
The Justice Department did not indicate how many of the more than 20,000 people it flagged in California had actually submitted a mail ballot.
It had argued that a restraining order was necessary to ensure that California did not impede prosecutors’ ability to enforce a federal law that makes it illegal for non-citizens to vote in federal elections.
But Carter said the Justice Department never explained why counting ballots would impair any prosecutions under the law, as states are not required to help the federal government investigate and prosecute crimes.
Apart from California, the Trump administration has sought to intervene in elections in two states that are home to competitive races.
In Alaska, the Justice Department last week asked a judge to prevent certification of election results if the Republican incumbent senator loses by a slim margin, alleging that the presence of another candidate with a similar name on the ballot could confuse voters.
Alaska has urged that the case be dismissed, arguing it has taken steps to distinguish the two candidates on the ballot.
In Washington state, the Justice Department on Oct 26 sent a letter asking officials not to count any ballots received from 400 voters it said may not be citizens.
Washington’s top election official said the timing of the request indicated it was intended to cast unfounded suspicion on election results.
California had 23 million registered voters as at December 2025, while Washington had five million registered voters as at 2024, state records show.
Voting rights activists have expressed concern that the federal government’s methods for scrutinising state voter lists to identify non-citizen voters risk wrongly flagging naturalised citizens for removal from the rolls. REUTERS

US hospitals and nursing homes are breeding grounds for deadly superbugs – CDC
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
00:45:34 UTC
09:45:34 KST

US hospitals and nursing homes are breeding grounds for deadly superbugs – CDC
More than four in five US deaths linked to drug-resistant infections involve pathogens commonly associated with hospitals and nursing homes, according to a new report from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).
The agency’s Antimicrobial Resistance Threats Report released this week draws on data from 2023 and estimates that 19 types of drug-resistant bacteria and fungi cause 9.7 million infections and 50,800 deaths annually in the US. Seven bacterial threats commonly associated with hospitals and nursing homes accounted for more than 42,000 of those deaths, along with nearly $12 billion in healthcare costs.
Antimicrobial resistance occurs when germs develop the ability to withstand drugs designed to kill them, making infections difficult or impossible to treat. Elderly people, those with weakened immune systems, and patients undergoing invasive medical procedures are particularly vulnerable.
Among the pathogens classified as urgent threats is Candida auris, a potentially deadly fungus that can resist multiple medications and survive on surfaces in healthcare facilities. It primarily affects seriously ill patients and can cause dangerous bloodstream infections.
A separate CDC study published in July found that reported cases of Candida auris more than doubled from 2022-2024, rising from 2,882 to 6,197. Most cases for which the type of medical facility was identified were detected in hospitals, including those that provide long-term treatment for seriously ill patients.
The CDC noted that many healthcare-associated infections are preventable, but much of the progress in combating drug resistance was lost during the Covid-19 pandemic, when staffing shortages, overcrowding, and disruptions to infection-control practices contributed to a rise in infections.
The warning comes as US hospitals face mounting financial and staffing pressures. A Harvard-led study published earlier this month found that 432 hospitals closed nationwide from 2010-2025, resulting in a net loss of 216 facilities and more than 24,000 beds.
Nursing homes are also struggling with bed and staffing shortages. An investigation in September by KFF Health News found that declining capacity forced some patients to remain hospitalized longer because suitable care facilities were unavailable.

Pakistan makes U-turn on Taiwan airline ban – media
Pakistan has restored overflight rights to two Taiwanese airlines after they stopped using its airspace three days earlier, according to AP, Bloomberg, and Dawn.
On Wednesday, Islamabad issued permits allowing Taiwan-based China Airlines and EVA Air to use Pakistani airspace until March 27, 2027, the outlets reported, citing official documents.
Hours earlier, Pakistani Defense Minister Khawaja Asif defended restrictions on Taiwanese carriers, citing Islamabad’s longstanding adherence to Beijing’s One-China policy.
“The aviation division follows the One-China policy – only mainland China is allowed,” Asif told Bloomberg. “We have permitted only Chinese airlines to fly over Pakistan.”
According to flight-tracking data, Taiwanese airlines began rerouting flights to avoid Pakistani airspace on October 25. Taipei condemned Islamabad for what it described as undermining Taiwan’s sovereignty and “politicizing and weaponizing airspace,” according to Taiwanese media.
Most countries, including the US and Russia, do not formally recognize Taiwan as an independent state. Beijing considers the self-governing island part of China and seeks reunification, preferably through peaceful means, but has not ruled out the use of force. Washington and several other Western governments maintain unofficial ties with Taiwan and supply it with weapons, drawing condemnation from China.
Pakistan’s restrictions reportedly went further than Beijing’s own rules, which permit some Taiwanese airline operations in mainland Chinese airspace.
China and Pakistan maintain close political and military ties, describing their relationship as an “all-weather strategic cooperative partnership.” China is Pakistan’s principal arms supplier, and Islamabad has consistently supported Beijing position on Taiwan.
Taiwanese airlines largely avoided Russian airspace after the escalation of the Ukraine conflict in 2022, although neither Moscow nor Taipei formally prohibited them from using it. Following the Pakistani restrictions, several Taiwan-Europe flights were rerouted through Russia.
According to Bloomberg, no country had previously imposed a blanket overflight ban on Taiwanese commercial airlines. In April, Seychelles, Mauritius, and Madagascar withdrew overflight clearances for Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te’s aircraft, forcing him to postpone a visit to Eswatini. Lai eventually made the trip in May.

CEO says plan is to file for bankruptcy after ending luxury never-ending cruise that left hundreds stranded
More than 200 passengers, mostly Americans, are stranded in Cambodia after the operator of a luxury U.S. cruise ship that was on a continuous around-the-world voyage ran out of money due to skyrocketing fuel costs.
Villa Vie Residences, the Florida-based operator of the MV Odyssey, said the war with Iran quadrupled fuel costs and forced it to suspend operations on Tuesday.
CEO Mikael Petterson told CBS News in a phone interview Wednesday that Villa Vie Residences was paying an average of $700 a ton for fuel before the war broke out in late February. Since then, it has been paying anywhere from $2,000 to $3,000 per ton.
The Odyssey uses between 700 and 800 tons per month in fuel, Petterson disclosed.
"When you divide it over 300 people on board, it's just backbreaking," Petterson told CBS News. "And this has been going on for nine months. We've tried to do everything we can do."
In a statement, Villa Vie Residences said the per cabin fuel costs rose from an average of $1,800 per month before the war to between $6,000 and $8,000.
The company was unwilling to pass those rising costs on to its passengers, Petterson said.
The Odyssey launched in October 2024 for a continuous around-the-world journey. At the time, passengers could become residents of the ship by purchasing a permanent cabin for several hundred thousand dollars. Some sold their homes to do so. At the time, they were given a 15-year minimum guarantee of residency aboard the Odyssey.
The Odyssey attempted to counter the spiking fuel prices by slowing down its itinerary and spending five or six days in each port "hoping that things would come to a close in the Middle East," Petterson said, but it wasn't enough.
"For us, when our monthly expenses go up from $400,000 to $2 million, where are we going to get the $1.6 million?" Petterson asked.
The Villa Vie Residences CEO said that the ship ran out of money as it searched for a financial partner, and the plan is now to file for Chapter 11 bankruptcy.
"We've borrowed money, we've stretched our payrolls as far as we can, and we're at a point where it's just at a breaking point where we need capitalization," Petterson said.
Passenger Benjamin Schatz thought the MV Odyssey would be his forever home.
"Honestly, right now, I'm in denial and in shock, and I'm heartbroken," Schatz, a retiree, told CBS News.
CBS News met Schatz in April 2025 for a story featuring Villa Vie Residences. At that point, he had been living on the ship for about one year. On Wednesday, he was given just hours to pack up his life and leave.
Said Schatz: "There are people now who are homeless and who have very little money and don't know what they're going to do."

Technology, U.S. Militarism, and Ethics: A Virtual Roundtable
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
00:24:06 UTC
09:24:06 KST

by Jing Xu (University of Washington)
How do technology and U.S. militarism shape one another from the past to the present, and what ethical responsibilities arise for researchers, technology workers, and the public? American Anthropologist organized the roundtable to address these urgent questions. This roundtable features Catherine Lutz, Lucy Suchman, and Roberto González in a discussion moderated by Jing Xu and Yang Zhan, associate editors of the journal. The discussion traced the historical expansion of U.S. militarism, the role of science and technology, and shifting cultural beliefs and political economy. It examined how militarization operates abroad and through everyday infrastructures at home, how the emotion of fear and claims of technological neutrality shape militarization processes, and what AI and automated systems mean for civilian harm and accountability. The speakers also reflected on their sources of hope in research and advocacy within and beyond academia.
