Monumental building, silver coins discovered at medieval city Rusokastro
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
12:56:13 UTC
21:56:13 KST

Monumental building, silver coins discovered at medieval city Rusokastro
Thursday 29 October 2026 13:09
Thursday, 29 October 2026, 13:09
PHOTO Regional History Museum in Burgas
Font size
A monumental building, 7.60 metres wide and of still unknown length, has been uncovered near the inner southern fortress wall. It is the latest archaeological discovery of the year made by archaeologists from Burgas at the medieval city of Rusokastro, the Regional Historical Museum in Burgas (RIM-Burgas) has announced.
The walls are 1.1 metres thick and built of stone bonded with abundant mortar. The inner surfaces of the building’s walls are heavily coated with pink waterproof mortar. This suggests that the structure was used as a water reservoir or a storehouse for food supplies. It most likely represents the ground floor of a building located in the city’s central quarter, with a second, residential floor presumed to have stood above it.
A large number of portable archaeological finds have also been unearthed, including silver coins minted under Bulgarian Tsar Ivan Alexander, Venetian silver grosso coins known as matapanes, copper coins and many other artefacts. These are now being cleaned in the restoration workshop of the Burgas museum.
Rusokastro is included on the list of priority national sites receiving state funding to support cultural tourism in Bulgaria.

Naval drones sink Greek container ship sailing from Israel off Bulgaria's coast
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
12:56:06 UTC
21:56:06 KST

A Greek-owned container ship chartered by Israeli shipping company ZIM sank in the Black Sea after being struck by unmanned surface vessels off the coast of Bulgaria on Wednesday, Bulgarian authorities said, in the latest attack on commercial shipping amid growing concerns over the spillover effects of the Russia-Ukraine war.
The Liberian-flagged CONTSHIP JET was carrying 421 shipping containers from Haifa's Gulf Port in Israel to the Romanian port of Constanța when it was attacked while passing through Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone, outside the country's territorial waters.
All 18 crew members, including 14 Filipinos and four Ukrainians, were rescued and safely transported to the Bulgarian port of Varna.
The Bulgarian government said it had received advance warning of the attack, believed to be connected to the war between Russia and Ukraine, but was unable to prevent it.
Footage published by a Bulgarian news website showed one of the unmanned surface vessels approaching the container ship moments before impact.
The ship sustained severe damage in the attack and subsequently sank, according to Bulgarian authorities.
The identity of those responsible remains unclear. Initial assessments suggest the vessel was not targeted because of its connection to Israel, although investigators have yet to establish a motive.
The incident has heightened concerns about the safety of commercial shipping in the western Black Sea, where attacks involving aerial and maritime drones have become increasingly frequent.
At least six vessels have been attacked by aerial or unmanned surface drones off Bulgaria's coast this month, leaving approximately 25 people dead, according to reports. The attacks have raised fears that the conflict between Russia and Ukraine is increasingly threatening shipping routes beyond the immediate war zone.
ZIM confirmed that the damaged vessel was chartered by the company but was not part of its owned fleet.
"A small container ship carrying a limited number of containers, which ZIM charters but does not own, was struck by an unmanned surface vessel in the Black Sea," the company said in a statement.
"All crew members were safely evacuated, and the expected financial damage, according to a preliminary assessment, is minimal."
The company said it was working to secure a replacement vessel and maintain service to its customers.
"To the best of our knowledge, several similar incidents involving vessels in the area have occurred over the past month," ZIM added.
Oren Caspi, chairman of ZIM's workers' union, said the attack underscored the importance of maintaining Israeli control over the shipping company amid growing geopolitical instability.
"In a reality of boycotts and security threats, in a world of political instability, we must keep ZIM Israeli," Caspi said.
"Much remains unknown about this extraordinary attack, and we are still learning the details."
Although Bulgaria does not share a land border with Russia or Ukraine, its position on the western Black Sea places it along important commercial shipping routes connecting the region to major Russian and Ukrainian ports.
The Black Sea has become a key theater of the Russia-Ukraine war, with unmanned aerial vehicles and explosive-laden maritime drones increasingly used in attacks on naval and maritime targets.
Such incidents have become more frequent in recent months, affecting Eastern European countries and shipping corridors previously considered relatively secure.
At least 45 merchant vessels have been attacked over the past 12 months in parts of the Black Sea that had not previously been classified as high-risk areas, according to figures cited in the report.
The latest sinking highlights the growing risks facing civilian shipping in the region, where commercial vessels continue to operate amid an expanding threat from unmanned weapons.
While there is no indication that the CONTSHIP JET was targeted because of its Israeli commercial connection, the attack adds to concerns among shipping operators about the safety of Black Sea routes and the potential for further disruption to international trade.

Volkswagen logs Q3 operating loss of €5.86 billion on Porsche writedown
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
12:54:00 UTC
21:54:00 KST

VW logs €5.86 billion Q3 operating loss on Porsche writedown
October 29, 2026
The Volkswagen Group on Thursday posted its worst quarterly numbers in more than a decade.
The company reported an operating loss of €5.86 billion (roughly $6.53 billion) during July, August and September. One-off costs, not least a massive writedown in its stake in struggling sister company Porsche, explained the vast bulk of the losses.
The world's second-largest carmaker is battling mounting competition from and falling demand in the core Chinese market.
It is pursuing a major restructuring and downsizing program, trying to bolster falling profit margins, and executives said the difficulties highlighted the urgency of this process.
"The nine-month results make one thing clear: We cannot afford to lose any time. We must act quickly and decisively," chief financial officer Arno Antlitz said in a video statement.
What were the main takeaways from VW's Q3 figures?
The results were the latest reminder of the pressure on VW — and the wider German and Western automotive industry — to react to increasing competition in China, high costs and practical difficulties moving towards electric car production, and unpredictable and rising tariff burdens, thanks in no small part to US President Donald Trump.
Here are some of the key Q3 figures:
- An operating loss of €5.86 billion, compared to €1.3 billion in same quarter last year
- It's the company's worst single quarterly loss since the height of the "Dieselgate" emissions scandal in 2015
- Sales revenue dipped 6.3% year-on-year, to €75.3 billion
- Deliveries to customers, unit sales, and unit production numbers all dipped by roughly 15% as the company starts to reduce production levels, trying to adjust to falling demand
And here are some of the key year-to-date 9-month figures:
- Sales revenue of €233.4 billion was broadly comparable to 2025's figure of €238.7 billion
- But vehicle unit sales, at 5.9 million, are 11% lower than 6.6 million last year — meaning the group is selling fewer cars, at higher prices
- The company's order intake for new cars rose 4% year-on-year, and by 39% for battery electric vehicles (BEVs)
- Operating profit lies at just €0.1 billion, compared with €5.4 billion a year ago
- But VW said 'special items' amounting to €8.7 billion primarily explain this massive dip
- Non-cash writedowns on Porsche assets worth €6.4 billion were the largest portion of this
How did investors respond?
VW shares were already at their lowest levels in well over 10 years prior to Thursday's announcements, after months of difficult headlines and the ongoing plans to shed tens of thousands of jobs and reduce production capacities.
Perhaps as a result of this, the stock dipped briefly as markets opened and the news was published, but then started to rally as the day progressed.
By midday in Frankfurt, VW shares had climbed by 2% compared to their prices at the start of trading on the DAX.
What are VW's downsizing plans?
CEO Oliver Blume plans to shed around 100,000 jobs across the group, which includes the Audi and Porsche brands, in the coming years though a combination of layoffs and not replacing departing or retiring personnel.
Multiple factors are contributing to this. They include increased competition from Chinese manufacturers, falling revenues in China, changeable US auto tariffs under President Donald Trump, different staffing requirements when manufacturing electric cars and difficulties moving towards making and selling more electric cars at the pace once designated by political leaders.
Up to four plants in Germany could face closure as part of the plan, which has met with considerable union resistance and could lead to strikes starting next year.
CFO Antlitz said the figures showed the urgency underlying these plans, saying the company needed to increase its profit margins by 2030 to solidify its finances.
Antlitz said the operating return on sales was only 3.8% in the first nine months of the year, even before the one-off writedowns hitting the bottom line.
"That is not enough in the long term," he said.
As part of its restructuring program, the VW Group aims to restore an operating profit margin of between 8-10% by 2030.
This year, amid one-off costs now totaling in the region of €10 billion, it expects a profit margin of no more than 1%, compared to prior forecasts in the region of 5%.

The government has allocated €7.3 million to increase the salaries of rescue workers and police officers, mainly those who are "lower-paid frontline employees," Minister of the Interior Igor Taro (Eesti 200) said on Thursday.
Speaking at the government's weekly press conference, he said rescue workers, police officers, border guards and emergency response operators at the Emergency Response Center are set to benefit from the funding boost.
"The government has allocated €7.3 million to our area of administration for pay raises. Salaries will increase in 3,764 positions from the beginning of next year," he said. In total, almost 8,000 people work in the ministry's area of administration.
"All of them deserve fair pay for their work. But the state's financial resources are limited, and this requires clear choices," Taro said.
"We are not distributing this additional money evenly as a percentage increase, but directing it primarily to lower-paid frontline employees," he explained.
Rescue workers will receive the largest pay raise, with their salaries increasing by €140 per month, Taro said. This means the minimum salary for a rescue worker will rise by nearly 9 percent and the average salary by 8 percent.
"This will bring the average salary of rescue workers to approximately 85 percent of the Estonian average. This is a necessary step forward, but it cannot be considered sufficient," the interior minister acknowledged. The average salary was €2,092 in 2025.
Taro said the minimum salary for a police officer will rise by 4.4 percent, the average salary of a patrol police officer will rise above the Estonian average, and the minimum salary of an emergency response operator at the Emergency Response Center will rise by nearly 5 percent.
He added that SMIT technicians and customer support specialists will also receive pay raises. "The pay raise will be €90 per month," Taro said.
"The pay raise also covers the immediate supervisors of frontline employees who themselves perform operational duties. Other managers' salaries will not increase. Salaries at the Ministry of the Interior will not increase," he said.

Russian general who ordered destruction of Skovoroda Museum to be tried in absentia
A Russian lieutenant general originally from the city of Chuhuiv in Kharkiv Oblast who is accused of directing a missile strike on the Hryhorii Skovoroda National Literary Memorial Museum will be tried in absentia.
Source: Prosecutor General's Office
Details: Regional media outlet Suspilne Kharkiv reported that the individual in question is Oleg Makovetsky, Commander of the Russian 6th Air and Air Defence Forces Army.
The investigation found that he knew full well that he was attacking a monument of Ukrainian culture rather than a military target. He issued a combat order for its destruction. Law enforcement officers have established the entire chain of transmission of the order through the commanders of the aviation division and the fighter aviation wing.
Makovetsky will be tried for violating the laws and customs of war, committed as part of a premeditated conspiracy by a group of individuals. He faces up to 15 years' imprisonment or a life sentence.
The museum in Skovorodynivka is a large memorial complex of monuments dating back to the 18th century, dedicated to the life and work of the famous Ukrainian philosopher and poet Hryhorii Savych Skovoroda. It was founded in 1972.
The museum collection comprises several thousand exhibits, including some of the philosopher's personal belongings, editions of his works, academic and literary works about him, books by ancient, medieval and modern philosophers and poets studied by Hryhorii Skovoroda, ethnographic artefacts, as well as paintings, graphic works and sculptures dedicated to him. Skovoroda's grave is near the main building.
Strike on the museum in Skovorodynivka
In May 2022, a Russian missile hit the roof of the building, causing a massive fire.
At that time, the missile struck beneath the roof of the building, igniting a fire that engulfed the entire museum. The 35-year-old son of the museum director, who had stayed behind to guard the premises overnight, suffered injuries. He was pulled from under the rubble and taken to hospital.
Only the statue of the philosopher survived the missile strike, becoming a distinctive symbol of resilience. Later, museum staff collected shards of pottery, metal fragments and charred books.
In 2024, the Security Service of Ukraine identified who had ordered the destruction of the Skovoroda Museum. It turned out to be Ivan Panchenko, commander of the 159th Fighter Aviation Regiment of the Western Military District of the Russian Armed Forces. Law enforcement officers notified him of the charges in absentia.
Last year, restorers managed to reconstruct 27 of the museum's exhibits.
In May 2026, a Russian drone damaged the protective shelter covering the building of the Hryhorii Skovoroda Museum.

Asian Cybersecurity in the Age of AI and Quantum Computing
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
12:30:00 UTC
21:30:00 KST

It was immediately apparent to habitués of Singapore International Cyber Week (SICW) that this year’s edition – the 11th, which ran from October 12-15 – was going to be different. Just days before the opening, on October 9, Taira Masaaki, who heads the Liberal Democratic Party’s cybersecurity strategy headquarters, told an emergency party meeting that Japan was in “a state of emergency in cyberspace.” More than 20 major Japanese companies had disclosed attacks in the preceding weeks. A ransomware attack on IDC Frontier, SoftBank’s cloud subsidiary, on October 7 took down systems at 495 companies and local governments.
It is unclear whether artificial intelligence (AI) directed any of those attacks. However, what was clear was that AI was the frisson that changed – perhaps for good – the tone and tenor of discussions at the plenaries, the closed sessions, and the corridor conversations at SICW. It has perhaps altered permanently the nature of discourse at all cyber forums of equal scale and standing that aspire to similar convening power.
What follows are thoughts and takeaways on where we should go from here.
Companies With the Power of States
U.S. AI companies such as OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic were in the room this year at SICW. It would have been useful to also have had some of the large Chinese AI firms present in order to get a sense of the alternative approaches. But regardless of their country of origin, some of these firms wield the power of states, and of powerful states for that matter. Their models automate tasks, and as we have seen in 2026, that increasingly includes cyber attacks. As AI agents become increasingly autonomous, the infrastructure underpinning them becomes an increasingly attractive target for cyberattacks.
Yet the companies developing these technologies and governments see different elements of the threat. A government can monitor attacks on its own networks and critical infrastructure, whilst frontier AI labs and major cloud providers can detect patterns of malicious activity across their customers and services. Neither has the complete picture. Ransomware is a clear example of where this matters. If these different sources of intelligence can be brought together, it would make it easier to spot emerging threats and understand how attackers are operating in order to disrupt attacks before they spread.
This is also changing how governments work with industry. Traditionally, governments set cybersecurity requirements, consulted industry, and expected or legislated that companies comply. However, frontier AI presents a far more complicated problem, which changes the dynamic. The companies who develop advanced AI systems possess technical knowledge, operational experience, and insights into emerging threats that governments cannot easily replicate.
The dichotomy here lies in the fact that while governments are considering how AI companies should be regulated, they are increasingly reliant on the technology and the expertise those same companies have. This means that the companies themselves have considerable influence over the decisions governments are trying to make about them.
Australia’s 2026 cyber threat assessment, released in October, illustrates what is at stake perfectly. The Australian Signals Directorate (ASD) warned that AI has been enabling malicious actors to identify vulnerabilities and carry out attacks – conduct espionage, steal money, and disrupt systems – at greater speed, scale, and sophistication. ASD Director General Abigail Bradshaw warned that frontier AI models had “redefined” the threat facing Australia, making further disruption to essential services increasingly likely.
The report pointed to emerging risks from the unintended behavior of AI agents, a problem that Australia has very publicly been managing over the past few months. Furthermore, it stated that there have been over 4,400 notifications to Australian organizations about possible malicious activity over the past year, which is an increase of almost 80 percent from 2025.
Bradshaw went on to state that ASD had been working directly with frontier AI companies, including OpenAI, to establish new early-warning protocols around emerging model capabilities and their potential misuse. These arrangements have also been shared with other AI labs and Five Eyes intelligence partners. This is significant as it demonstrates intelligence agencies need to work with AI frontier labs before new capabilities are widely deployed, rather than responding to the threats that they appear to increasingly unleash. The question is how do governments secure that cooperation while retaining independence and authority to regulate those same companies.
This is where Singapore’s approach becomes particularly interesting.
It seems likely that Singapore’s approach will (as so often is the case in these matters) be measured and shorn of histrionics – relying on the assumption that the cooperative approach can work, at least in the first instance. Minister for Digital Development and Information Josephine Teo, who is at the helm of the cybersecurity portfolio, while noting the safeguards put in place by frontier AI companies, said that these were insufficient, given the risks posed by increasingly capable systems. She also told Parliament days before SICW opened that Singapore does not currently require frontier AI developers to give the government access to their models, warning that a rigid requirement could be counterproductive if it makes companies limit cooperation or information-sharing. The non-coercive approach was on view when Anthropic, in the course of opening its Singapore office, signed an MOU covering AI safety, security, and model evaluation at Cyber Week.
Filling the Quantum Gap
Amid all the talk of AI, it was easy to miss some of the deeper signals and concerns emanating from conversations at SICW.
Post-quantum cryptography was the quieter theme, perhaps because technically, it does not have a date attached to it. A quantum computer able to break today’s public-key encryption does not yet exist, but there was general agreement that that day – “Q-Day” – can be glimpsed on the horizon.
The problem here is that we do not need to reach Q-Day for the risks to eventuate. Policymakers and technical experts across the region should be considering it now, rather than assuming that their successors will carry the can. The risk to secrets is already real, because data stolen now can be stored and decrypted later. Organizations holding information that needs to remain confidential for years to come should already be planning their migration to quantum-resistant cryptography. Even after this is completed, systems will require continual monitoring and updating as the technology and subsequent threat evolves.
All this also means the need for discussions and coordination not just within but across regions. Australia has recommended that companies complete the transition by the end of 2030. Singapore has set 2031 as the target for critical infrastructure and 2035 for everyone else. At surface level these timelines appear reasonable, but international networks and supply chains do not operate within national boundaries. If one country, or one part of a network, has migrated while another has not, the security communications and data shared between them remains exposed. Therefore, industry and governments need to think beyond their own migration deadlines and consider how different timelines will impact the networks and services that connect them.
The Politics of Getting Everyone in the Room
Despite these uncertainties, there were positives that underlined SICW’s convening power. The event brought Washington, Beijing, and Moscow into the same building, alongside ASEAN’s cyber ministers, the United Nations, and, this year, senior officials from Anthropic and OpenAI. No other annual cyber convention meeting assembles all of those layers at once.
The interactions should not be sugar-coated. Officials from the EU walked out of the High-Level Panel on Diplomacy, which featured a Russian official (Dmitrii Bukin from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs), just as they had done in 2025. (Some did, however, leave staffers at the end of the room to take notes). And there were occasional sharp moments from the United States, for example when Sean Cairncross, the United States national cyber director, used the plenary to attack digital authoritarianism. Chinese officials chose not to respond directly, and it does not appear that others (including ASEAN states) shared these sentiments.
SICW is not – at least not yet – a showpiece for great power cyber grandstanding. Singapore officials may well want to keep the tone even-handed. At the same time, they may value balance, with middle and even smaller powers having a seat at the table. After all, Singapore officials repeatedly averred in and about SICW that the decisions in this realm cannot be left to the major powers and the frontier AI companies, and that cyber diplomacy has to involve all. The program reflected that, with delegations from Timor-Leste to Tuvalu.
Australia is on the same page and is playing a role in this respect. When it helped set up the Pacific Cyber Security Operational Network in 2018, the point was to give every Pacific incident responder a counterpart to call, and most of those calls now go island to island rather than through Canberra. Tuvalu shows how far the layers have joined. The Falepili Union of 2023 gave Australia a security role in a country of 11,000 people, and ground has since been broken on the Tuvalu Vaka cable, a US$56 million link delivered with Google and backed by Australia, Japan, New Zealand, Taiwan, and the United States.
What to Do Before 2027
Cyber diplomacy has enough rules. It needs more follow-through.
The common thread is that the technology now moves faster than the policy written to govern it. It would be tempting therefore to suggest that new norms are needed. But our conclusion from the week is that the region does not need a new set of rules. The norms already agreed at the United Nations and endorsed within ASEAN (in the case of the GGE, the Group of Governmental Experts, with the permanent mechanism established by the OEWG also being welcomed by the body) are adequate to the task. What is missing is implementation, and that is work small and middle powers are well placed to lead.
What is actually required is picking a small number of things the countries in the room can do together, and doing them before the next SICW. Three concrete steps follow from this year’s discussions.
First, align post-quantum migration deadlines across shared infrastructure, or at least agree which systems must migrate on the earlier timeline whoever owns them. Second, build information-sharing arrangements with the large technology firms that give governments the view of telemetry they cannot collect themselves, on terms that survive a change of chief executive. Third, agree on a common ASEAN vocabulary for AI risk that carries weight and meaning beyond the region, so that a regulator in Jakarta and a regulator in Canberra mean the same thing when they describe risk.
Singapore chairs ASEAN in 2027, which makes the next SIWC especially significant. For Australia and Singapore it is the first real test of whether small and middle powers can set a cyber agenda rather than hold a seat while others set it.
The rules are written. The next 12 months will show who is prepared to carry them out.

NASA discovers Jupiter’s invisible shield is more complex than Earth’s
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
12:26:25 UTC
21:26:25 KST

NASA discovers Jupiter’s invisible shield is more complex than Earth’s
NASA’s Juno spacecraft has uncovered Jupiter’s surprisingly complex defense against the solar wind, revealing physics that could help explain the power of exploding stars.
- Date:
- October 29, 2026
- Source:
- University of Iowa
- Summary:
- NASA’s Juno spacecraft has discovered that Jupiter uses a surprisingly complex system of powerful plasma waves and multiple shock regions to defend against the solar wind. The findings reveal major differences between Jupiter and Earth and could help scientists understand the enormous shock waves produced by exploding stars.
- Share:
NASA's Juno spacecraft has uncovered remarkable new details about how Jupiter withstands the constant stream of high-energy particles flowing from the Sun. The findings reveal that the solar system's largest planet relies on a much more complex system of plasma waves and shock regions than Earth does.
Led by scientists at the University of Iowa, the research provides the most detailed observations yet of Jupiter's bow shock, an invisible boundary where particles from the Sun encounter the planet's magnetic environment. The discovery reveals important differences in how Jupiter and Earth respond to these incoming particles.
Beyond Jupiter, the results could also help scientists understand some of the most powerful events in the universe, including the extreme shock waves associated with exploding stars.
How Jupiter Protects Itself From the Solar Wind
The Sun continuously releases a stream of electrically charged particles called the solar wind. These particles travel through space at tremendous speeds, often faster than the speed at which sound waves move through the surrounding plasma. When the solar wind approaches a planet with a magnetic field, it encounters a boundary known as the bow shock.
At Earth, this boundary plays an important protective role. It slows and heats the incoming particles, helping redirect much of the solar wind around the planet. Without this process, more harmful particles could reach Earth's atmosphere, potentially making conditions less favorable for life.
Jupiter also has a bow shock, but its enormous size, powerful magnetic field, and gaseous composition make it a particularly interesting place to study how these boundaries behave. Scientists have long wanted to understand whether Jupiter handles the solar wind differently from Earth and what those differences might reveal about other objects throughout the universe.
Scientists Discover a More Complex Defense System
Using measurements from Juno, researchers discovered that Jupiter relies on plasma waves with multiple frequencies to slow and heat incoming solar particles. These different frequencies, known as "harmonics," create a more elaborate wave pattern than the one typically observed at Earth.
The process can be compared to music. Just as several notes played together produce a richer sound than a single note, plasma waves containing multiple frequencies can interact with incoming particles in more complex ways. This allows Jupiter's bow shock to transfer energy to more particles, heating them and reducing their speed.
Earth's bow shock, by comparison, primarily uses plasma waves concentrated around a single frequency. That simpler arrangement is generally sufficient for the conditions encountered near our planet.
"Jupiter has found its own way to deal with the solar wind, through plasma waves that are stronger and exhibit richer harmonic structures," says Jayasri Joseph, a postdoctoral researcher in the Department of Physics and Astronomy at Iowa and the study's corresponding author. "That's important because if you have multiple frequencies, you can heat more particles in the solar wind and slow them down."
Jupiter Has an Extra Line of Defense
The researchers identified another striking difference in how the two planets interact with the solar wind.
Before incoming particles reach Jupiter's main bow shock, they can encounter smaller shock structures called shocklets. These additional regions help slow the solar wind before it arrives at the primary shock boundary.
Earth's bow shock, in contrast, generally serves as the main region where the incoming solar wind is slowed and redirected. Jupiter's additional shock structures reveal a more complicated process for managing the energy carried by solar particles.
"Earth does not need to take these extra steps to handle the solar wind because the impact isn't as powerful," says Bill Kurth, a research scientist in Iowa's Department of Physics and Astronomy and a coauthor of the study.
Kurth has participated in NASA's Juno mission since the spacecraft launched in 2011.
What Jupiter Can Teach Us About Exploding Stars
Although these observations focus on Jupiter, their significance could extend far beyond our solar system.
Shock waves occur throughout the universe, particularly in environments where enormous amounts of energy are released. Some of the most extreme examples are found in supernova remnants, the expanding clouds of material left behind when certain dying stars explode.
These cosmic shock waves are vastly more powerful than those encountered near Jupiter. However, the physical processes that control how energy moves through plasma share important similarities. By examining Jupiter's bow shock in unprecedented detail, scientists can investigate mechanisms that would be much harder to measure directly around distant stars.
"Because even more powerful shocks occur around astrophysical objects such as supernova remnants, Jupiter's bow shock offers a nearby natural laboratory for exploring and for understanding how nature converts enormous amounts of flow energy into heat and energetic particles," Joseph says.
Understanding these processes could improve scientific models of how shock waves transfer energy, heat particles, and shape environments across the universe.
NASA's Juno Makes Unprecedented Measurements
The breakthrough was made possible by observations Juno collected in December 2024. The NASA spacecraft has been orbiting Jupiter since July 2016, providing researchers with an extraordinary opportunity to investigate the giant planet and its surrounding environment.
A key part of the discovery came from the Juno Waves instrument, which was designed and built by physicists at the University of Iowa. The instrument measures electric and magnetic wave activity, allowing scientists to study the behavior of plasma around Jupiter.
Earlier spacecraft had detected the presence of bow shocks at outer planets, but they lacked the measurements needed to reveal the detailed structure of the plasma waves involved. Juno's observations have now provided a much clearer picture of how these waves behave at Jupiter.
The findings were published online on July 31 in Nature Communications in a study titled "Plasma wave observations from Juno spacecraft at the Jovian bow shock."
Research Team and NASA Support
Additional contributors from the University of Iowa included Allison Jaynes, an associate professor in the Department of Physics and Astronomy, along with Jeremy Faden and Chris Piker, who provide research support in the same department.
The international research team also included Lynn Wilson III of NASA Goddard Space Flight Center; John Connerney of NASA Goddard Space Flight Center and the Space Research Corporation; Frederic Allegrini of the Southwest Research Institute and the University of Texas-San Antonio; Rob Wilson of the University of Colorado-Boulder; Ali Sulaiman of the University of Minnesota; Scott Boltion and Robert Ebert of the Southwest Research Institute; and Barry Mauk of the Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory.
NASA provided funding for the research.
Story Source:
Materials provided by University of Iowa. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- J. Joseph, W. S. Kurth, L. B. Wilson, J. E. P. Connerney, F. Allegrini, R. J. Wilson, A. H. Sulaiman, R. W. Ebert, J. B. Faden, C. W. Piker, A. N. Jaynes, B. H. Mauk, S. J. Bolton. Plasma wave observations from Juno spacecraft at the Jovian bow shock. Nature Communications, 2026; 17 (1) DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-76223-x

Ukraine to Co-Found New International Defence Bank With Canada and European Partners
Ukraine will become a co-founder of the new Defence, Security and Resilience Bank (DSRB), joining Canada and eight other countries in establishing the international institution, Canada’s Department of Finance announced on October 26.
Canadian Finance and National Revenue Minister François-Philippe Champagne confirmed that Canada, Albania, Belgium, Greece, Latvia, Luxembourg, Romania, Türkiye, and Ukraine will jointly establish the DSRB.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
The participating countries are expected to sign the bank’s Articles of Agreement in Luxembourg on November 30, 2026. The DSRB will be headquartered in Canada and operate a European hub in Luxembourg.
The bank is being created to mobilize public and private capital for defense, security, and resilience projects among participating countries. Its mandate will include sovereign financing, expansion of defense-industrial capacity, critical supply chains, and eligible defense procurement.
The DSRB is also intended to address financing gaps faced by governments and defense companies, including small- and medium-sized enterprises. Financing will be available to eligible members on equal terms, regardless of their size or economic capacity.
Canada stated that the bank will seek a AAA credit rating backed by participating countries, allowing it to reduce borrowing costs, expand access to long-term financing, and attract additional commercial investment into the defense sector.
“In an increasingly uncertain and divided world, Canada is working to bring together like-minded partners to mobilize and deploy private capital in support of collective security,” Champagne stated.
Membership will remain open to other allies and close partners that share the bank’s objectives.
The November signing follows negotiations on the Articles of Agreement held in Montréal in spring 2026 and a joint declaration issued by participating countries in July. Canada expects the DSRB to become fully operational in 2027.
The new DSRB would add another financing mechanism for defense support involving Ukraine. UNITED24 Media previously reported that NATO’s Prioritized Ukraine Requirements List (PURL) allows allies to finance US-made weapons requested by Kyiv, with the mechanism supplying 95% of Ukraine’s Patriot missiles one year after its launch.

The incident follows another Russian attack on a bird care facility in the Kyiv region. On October 7, a Russian attack involving drones and ballistic missiles destroyed the Sadiba Nyushanik bird rehabilitation center in the Vyshhorod district, according to its co-founder, Iryna Snopko.
The strike destroyed the center’s bird treatment facility, chicken coop, and quail enclosure, along with equipment and feed stored on the premises.
“We were hit. The bird treatment facility, chicken coop, and quail enclosure burned down. There were birds and a cat inside, as well as all the equipment and feed,” Snopko said.
The Sadiba Nyushanik center specialized in the rescue and rehabilitation of birds of prey and waterfowl, caring for species including storks, swans, owls, hawks, and kestrels.
However, birds are not the only animals affected by Russian attacks on Ukraine. In a separate incident, an overnight Russian strike hit the Loving Hearts animal shelter in Velykodolynske, Odesa region, killing three dogs and 10 cats, according to the shelter. The fate of several other animals remained uncertain following the attack.
As the strike unfolded, the shelter’s owner managed to open the enclosures, allowing the animals to escape. However, it remained unclear how many had survived.
As of February 24, 2026, more than 6 million animals had been killed as a result of the war, while more than 20% of the country’s protected natural areas had sustained damage.

Einstein's equations may explain the universe without dark energy
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
12:07:58 UTC
21:07:58 KST

Einstein's equations may explain the universe without dark energy
- Date:
- October 29, 2026
- Source:
- University of California - Davis
- Summary:
- Mathematicians have uncovered what they argue is a fundamental flaw in the standard model of the universe, potentially challenging the need for dark energy. Their calculations suggest that the mathematical framework used to describe cosmic expansion is inherently unstable and that the universe could accelerate naturally under Einstein's original theory of gravity. The findings also raise surprising questions about whether our location in the universe is as ordinary as scientists have long assumed.
- Share:
Mathematicians are raising a major challenge to one of modern cosmology's most widely accepted explanations: the idea that dark energy is driving the accelerating expansion of the universe.
A study published in Proceedings of the Royal Society A presents mathematical findings that researchers at the University of California, Davis, say reveal a fundamental instability in the standard model of the expanding universe. Their calculations suggest that cosmic acceleration could emerge naturally from Einstein's equations, potentially eliminating the need to invoke mysterious dark energy.
The work challenges the Lambda-cold dark matter model, the leading framework scientists use to describe the universe's evolution since the Big Bang. The researchers reached their conclusions by studying the Einstein-Euler equations, which combine Einstein's theory of general relativity with equations describing how fluids behave. Together, these mathematical tools help scientists investigate everything from galaxies and black holes to the expansion of the cosmos.
A Hidden Instability in Our Model of the Universe
To explain the problem, Blake Temple, the study's corresponding author and a distinguished professor emeritus of mathematics at UC Davis, offered a simple comparison: a pencil balanced vertically on its tip.
"All the forces are in balance when a pencil is standing on end, so it is a 'solution of the equations,'" he said. "But it's unstable. Any breath of air and it falls away."
According to Temple, the team's mathematical analysis shows that Friedmann spacetimes, which form the foundation of conventional models of cosmic expansion, are unstable at both small and large scales in the context of the Big Bang. He described the standard solution as exceptionally unstable.
"Unstable solutions in physics and science are considered not physical," Temple said. "You'll never observe them in nature."
This instability could have far-reaching consequences. If the universe naturally evolves away from the behavior predicted by these conventional models, its accelerating expansion might not require a separate form of energy to explain it. Instead, Temple argues, the answer could already be contained within Einstein's original theory of gravity.
"The instability of all Friedmann spacetimes to accelerated expansion suggests a simpler, more natural explanation for the acceleration of the universe than dark energy," he said.
Why Scientists Believe Dark Energy Is Expanding the Universe
For nearly three decades, dark energy has been the leading explanation for one of astronomy's most puzzling discoveries: the universe is not simply expanding, but its expansion is accelerating.
The concept has roots in Einstein's groundbreaking 1915 theory of general relativity, which describes gravity as the curvature of space and time. Einstein originally believed the universe was static, neither expanding nor contracting. To make his equations compatible with that assumption, he introduced a mathematical term that counteracted gravity, calling it the "cosmological constant."
That assumption changed after Edwin Hubble discovered evidence in 1929 that the universe was expanding. Einstein famously referred to his introduction of the cosmological constant as his "biggest blunder," since his original equations without the additional term could have predicted an expanding universe.
The cosmological constant returned to prominence in the 1990s, when astronomers discovered that cosmic expansion was speeding up. It became closely associated with dark energy, the name given to the unknown component thought to be responsible for this acceleration.
Today's standard cosmological framework builds on the Friedmann universe, a mathematical description in which space expands while matter remains evenly distributed across the cosmos at any given moment. This assumption of large-scale uniformity plays a central role in how scientists reconstruct the universe's history.
But Temple and his collaborators began questioning whether the underlying mathematics could remain stable, prompting them to investigate other possible explanations for the observed acceleration.
Could Einstein's Equations Explain Cosmic Acceleration?
The researchers initially considered whether a massive shockwave might help explain the universe's expansion and the unexpected acceleration associated with it.
"Our first idea was that maybe the universe was expanding because there was a shockwave, and the anomalous acceleration was the expanding wave behind that shockwave," Temple said. "Then we realized there's a family of self-similar solutions during the radiation epoch of the Big Bang, which might model that expanding wave."
In mathematics and physics, self-similar solutions describe patterns that retain their underlying structure when viewed at different scales. A familiar example is a fractal, in which similar shapes can appear at increasingly larger or smaller sizes.
The researchers identified a family of these solutions associated with the radiation-dominated period of the early universe, when radiation played a major role in determining how the cosmos evolved.
Building on their earlier work, they used a self-similar form of Einstein's equations to represent the standard cosmological model as a rest point, a mathematical state in which the system's defining variables remain unchanged. This approach allowed them to examine whether small departures from that state would disappear or grow over time.
Their analysis provided a mathematical framework for evaluating the stability of the standard model and, more broadly, Friedmann spacetimes during the matter-dominated era of the early universe, when matter became more influential than radiation.
A Mathematical Challenge to the Standard Big Bang Model
The results suggest that the conventional mathematical descriptions of the expanding universe are vulnerable to disturbances that grow rather than fade.
"We prove that, like Einstein's static model, the Friedmann spacetimes are all unstable to radial perturbation at large length scales," Temple said. "This appears to rule out the Lambda-cold dark matter model as a viable stable solution of the Einstein equations of general relativity, with or without dark energy."
Radial perturbations are disturbances that change with distance from a central point. In the researchers' mathematical framework, such changes can cause the behavior of an expanding universe to depart from the predictions of the standard Friedmann model.
"This means," he added, "that the Big Bang should generically look exactly like a Friedmann spacetime near the center of symmetry, but generically one should observe accelerations away from Friedmann far from the center."
In other words, the universe could behave much like the standard model predicts near a central region while exhibiting different expansion behavior farther away.
The researchers argue that this instability may offer a natural route to accelerated cosmic expansion without adding a cosmological constant or invoking dark energy. Their calculations indicate that the acceleration can emerge directly from the Einstein-Euler equations themselves.
The findings represent a theoretical challenge to standard cosmology rather than observational proof that dark energy is unnecessary. Establishing whether this alternative can describe the actual universe would require determining how well its predictions match astronomical observations.
Does the Universe Have a Special Location?
Beyond the dark energy question, the study also raises a more fundamental issue involving the Copernican principle.
Named after astronomer Nicolaus Copernicus, who helped overturn the belief that Earth sits at the center of the solar system, the principle holds that our location in the universe is not fundamentally special or privileged.
This assumption has become an important part of modern cosmology, supporting the view that the universe looks broadly similar when observed from different locations on sufficiently large scales.
The researchers' alternative mathematical framework introduces a center of spherical symmetry, raising questions about where an observer would need to be located for the model to agree with observations.
Temple argues that the Copernican principle must be applied consistently when evaluating competing explanations of the universe.
"Both the Lambda-cold dark matter model and a spherically symmetric spacetime produce a special place where we must lie for the model to be physically plausible," Temple said. "If this principle rules out one, it has to rule out the other."
The work opens another avenue for investigating why the universe's expansion is accelerating. Although dark energy remains a central component of the prevailing cosmological model, the researchers contend that the mathematics of general relativity may offer a different explanation for the same phenomenon.
If further theoretical and observational work supports their interpretation, it could lead to a significant reassessment of how scientists understand cosmic expansion and the mathematical foundations of the Big Bang.
The research received funding from the United Kingdom's Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council and the American Institute of Mathematics SQuaREs Program.
Story Source:
Materials provided by University of California - Davis. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- C. Alexander, B. Temple, Z. Vogler. The instability of critical and underdense Friedmann spacetimes at the Big Bang as an alternative to dark energy. Proceedings of the Royal Society A Mathematical Physical and Engineering Science, 2026; 482 (2338) DOI: 10.1098/rspa.2025.0912

BEIJING, Oct. 29 (Xinhua) -- The 20th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China concluded its fifth plenary session on Thursday in Beijing with a communique issued.
The following is the full text of the communique:
Communique of the Fifth Plenary Session of
the 20th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China
Adopted at the fifth plenary session of the 20th Central Committee
of the Communist Party of China on October 29, 2026
The 20th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China convened its fifth plenary session in Beijing from October 26 to 29, 2026.
A total of 162 members and 117 alternate members of the Central Committee attended the session. Members of the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection and leading officials from relevant departments were present at the meeting in a non-voting capacity. Some of our primary-level colleagues and a number of experts and scholars, serving as delegates to the 20th National Party Congress, also attended the meeting in a non-voting capacity.
The Political Bureau of the Central Committee presided over the meeting. Xi Jinping, General Secretary of the Central Committee, delivered an important address.
The Central Committee heard and discussed a report on the work of the Political Bureau, presented by Xi Jinping on behalf of the Political Bureau. They also deliberated and adopted the Resolution of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China on Certain Major Issues concerning Persevering with Full and Rigorous Party Self-Governance. Xi Jinping delivered explanatory remarks on the draft Resolution.
At the session, the Central Committee fully affirmed the work of the Political Bureau since the fourth plenary session of the 20th Central Committee. It was unanimously agreed that the Political Bureau has secured progress in the following respects: earnestly implementing the guiding principles from the Party's 20th National Congress and the plenary sessions of the 20th Central Committee; adhering to the general principle of pursuing progress while ensuring stability; fully and faithfully applying the new development philosophy on all fronts; implementing the Five-Sphere Integrated Plan and the Four-Pronged Comprehensive Strategy in a coordinated way; balancing domestic and international imperatives; ensuring both development and security; delivering tangible results in high-quality economic development; advancing socialist democracy and the rule of law; improving public communication and cultural work; ensuring the people's wellbeing and promoting ecological conservation; safeguarding national security and social stability; further strengthening full and rigorous Party self-governance; modernizing national defense and the armed forces; carrying out work related to Hong Kong, Macao, and Taiwan; and pursuing major-country diplomacy with Chinese characteristics. Thanks to these efforts, the 14th Five-Year Plan has been brought to a successful conclusion and the 15th Five-Year Plan period is off to a good start with new progress and results achieved in the cause of the Party and the country. It was also noted that, this year, we launched a study campaign on establishing and practicing the correct view of performance and celebrated the 105th anniversary of the Communist Party of China. These occasions have further harnessed the mighty force that stems from the entire Party and the whole nation forging ahead in unity.
Looking back on the Party's journey since its founding, the Central Committee pointed out at the session that the key to the success of the Communist Party of China in winning one victory after another lies in its pursuit of the high ideal of communism, its dedication to achieving lasting greatness for the Chinese nation, and its commitment to seeking happiness for the Chinese people and rejuvenation for the Chinese nation. During each historical period, the Party has attached great importance to its self-governance, had the courage to uphold truth and correct errors, and grown ever stronger by relying on its own efforts and the support of the people to resolve its own problems, ultimately emerging as the strong leadership core in the cause of the Party and the people. The Party advanced Party building as a great project and then a great new project in the periods of revolution, development, and reform, and it has made further progress in this regard in the new era since its 18th National Congress. During this course, the Party has found two answers to the question of how to escape the historical cycle of rise and fall: the people's oversight over government and the Party's self-reform. These are the unique discoveries of the Communist Party of China, and will forever stand out in the history of Marxist parties.
Participants at the session gave a highly positive assessment of the great achievements our Party has made in exercising full and rigorous self-governance in the new era. It was unanimously agreed that the Central Committee with Comrade Xi Jinping at its core demonstrated tremendous political courage and a strong sense of responsibility in confronting the grave situation marked by weak, hollow, and watered-down Party leadership, lax, superficial, and ineffective self-supervision and self-governance, as well as some startling problems within the Party. Staying firmly committed to full and rigorous Party self-governance, the Central Committee introduced the most stringent measures and dedicated continuous efforts to tackle all these prominent issues. As a result, the problem of lax and weak self-supervision and self-governance has been addressed at the root, unhealthy tendencies that had long gone unchecked have been curbed, deep-seated problems that had plagued the Party for years have been remedied, and serious dangers hidden within the Party, the state, and the military have been removed. The Party has thus grown stronger through revolutionary tempering. The endeavors to advance full and rigorous governance over the Party in the new era have broken new ground in the self-reform of our century-old Party and brought about historic achievements and transformations in the cause of the Party and the country. The Party and the people have thus seized the historic initiative in building a great party and a great country.
It was pointed out that as the Party endeavors to supervise, govern, develop, and strengthen itself in the new era, the Central Committee with Comrade Xi Jinping at its core has put forward a series of new ideas, new thinking, and new strategies in response to the major questions of our times -- what kind of long-term governing Marxist party we should build and how we should build it, thereby giving birth to Xi Jinping Thought on Party Building. This thought has enriched and developed Marxist theory on party building, and it represents a major achievement in advancing the Party's theoretical innovation through the integration of the basic tenets of Marxism with China's specific realities and its fine traditional culture. It stands as a crystallization of the practical experience and collective wisdom of the Party and the people. As an important component of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, it provides fundamental guidance and a road map for further advancing the great new project of Party building in the new era.
It was stressed that many favorable conditions are now in place for advancing full and rigorous Party self-governance, while we are also facing many new circumstances and new issues in this endeavor. Profound changes in global, national, and Party conditions have made the Party's tasks of uniting and leading the people in safeguarding China's sovereignty, security, and development interests, of uniting and leading the people in promoting reform and development and maintaining social harmony and stability, and of maintaining its advanced nature and integrity even more arduous. All this poses formidable challenges to the Party's governance and leadership capacity, the quality of its membership, and its resistance against corruption and moral decline under the new circumstances. Moreover, the "four tests" and "four dangers" confronting our Party are still protracted, complicated, and serious.
On this account, all of us in the Party must gain a deep understanding of the great significance of persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance from the strategic perspective of consolidating the Party's long-term governing position and realizing the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. We must build firm confidence, maintain resolve, and adopt higher standards and more concrete measures to carry forward the valuable experience of full and rigorous Party self-governance in the new era, handle and resolve the prominent problems in Party building, and consolidate and develop the sound political situation formed through Party self-supervision and self-governance.
It was stated that in persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance, we must uphold Marxism-Leninism, Mao Zedong Thought, Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Theory of Three Represents, and the Scientific Outlook on Development, fully implement Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and thoroughly study and apply Xi Jinping Thought on Party Building. Dedicated to fulfilling the Party's missions and tasks, we must act in line with the overall requirements for Party building in the new era, take the Party Constitution as our fundamental guide, maintain the Party's vanguard nature, and uphold the overall leadership of the Party and the centralized, unified leadership of the Party Central Committee. We must focus on enhancing the Party's capacity for long-term governance, preserving its advanced nature and integrity, and maintaining its close bond with the people. We must unwaveringly apply strict principles, improve the system of exercising full and rigorous Party self-governance, and take strengthening the Party politically as the overarching principle to advance Party building on all fronts. We must stimulate greater motivation, initiative, and creativity within the whole Party, continue working to purify, improve, renew, and excel ourselves, and constantly strengthen the Party's capacity for providing political leadership, giving theoretical guidance, organizing the people, and inspiring society. In doing so, we will see that the Party always remains a vibrant Marxist governing party that stays at the forefront of the times, enjoys the wholehearted support of the people, and is able to withstand all tests, and that it always remains the strong leadership core of the cause of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
At the session, the guiding principles for persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance were highlighted as follows: serving the Party's missions and tasks; taking strengthening the Party politically as the overarching principle; exercising rigorous governance across the board; adopting a problem-oriented approach; upholding fundamental principles and breaking new ground; adhering to a top-down approach; and running the Party according to regulations.
Systematic plans for persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance were also made at the session with the emphasis on strengthening the Party spirit of Communists; strictly practicing democratic centralism; cultivating high-caliber officials capable of shouldering the mission of national rejuvenation; building a well-knit organizational system characterized by cross-level alignment and effective implementation; improving conduct and tightening discipline on an ongoing basis; taking firm and coordinated action against corruption; running the Party with systems and regulations; refining Party and state oversight systems; and ensuring all responsibilities of Party self-supervision and self-governance are fulfilled in earnest.
It was pointed out that strengthening the Party spirit represents a fundamental task of our efforts to ensure full and rigorous Party self-governance. We must, therefore, encourage all Party members and officials to uphold the Party's nature and purpose, raise Party consciousness, have a better understanding of their identity as Party members and the Party's vanguard nature, and maintain a lifelong commitment to cultivating stronger Party spirit. We must also encourage them to devote efforts to strengthening ideals and convictions, forging strong loyalty to the Party, fostering deep affection for the people, always seeking truth from facts, building moral character, and preserving honesty and integrity. These efforts will help them to be loyal, upright, and responsible and always preserve the true political character of Communists. We must improve and implement the institutions of democratic centralism, giving full play to intraparty democracy while effectively practicing correct centralism. It was stated that strict management of officials is the key to full and rigorous Party self-governance. We must implement the Party's organizational line for the new era and apply stringent standards to the education, cultivation, selection, appointment, management, and oversight of officials. On this basis, we will build up the ranks of high-caliber officials with firm political commitment, outstanding professional competence, excellent work conduct, and strict discipline. Following sound guidelines in appointing officials, we should take targeted, well-designed measures to select and appoint officials, inspire officials to foster and act on the correct view of performance, enhance officials' competence in fulfilling their duties and breaking new ground, improve the training and selection of outstanding young officials, and strengthen management and oversight of officials, with a view to promoting the training, recruitment, and utilization of talented people across the board.
It was stated that Party organizations at all levels play the principal role in exercising full and rigorous Party self-governance. It is therefore essential to systematically advance the development of Party organizations at all levels and in all sectors to strengthen their political and organizational functions. This will help ensure that the Party's lines, principles, and policies, as well as the Party Central Committee's decisions and plans are implemented through well-coordinated, targeted, and effective efforts. More specifically, we should give play to the exemplary role of Party organizations of central Party and state organs, bolster the functions of local Party committees, take coordinated steps to improve primary-level Party organizations across all sectors, promote Party building in emerging sectors, build a strong contingent of Party members, and refine mechanisms to ensure alignment across different levels of Party organizations.
It was pointed out that improving conduct and tightening discipline are effective measures to advance full and rigorous Party self-governance. We must work in concert to enhance Party spirit, improve Party conduct, and tighten Party discipline, and integrate conduct improvement and discipline enforcement with anti-corruption measures. Drawing on the experience gained in advancing full and rigorous Party self-governance through conduct improvement efforts, we will ensure steady improvements in our conduct, supervise and govern the Party with strict discipline, and pool support and strength with a positive image. In practice, we will follow the Party's mass line in the new era, steadfastly implement the central Party leadership's eight-point decision on improving work conduct, put in consistent and sustained efforts to improve conduct, ensure more rigorous discipline enforcement, and make full use of discipline as a guide, restraint, guarantee, and incentive.
It was noted that taking integrated steps to ensure that officials do not have the audacity, opportunity, or desire to commit corruption is both an important strategy for full and rigorous Party self-governance and a fundamental guideline for our fight against corruption. The Party tolerates no corruption, as it has no special interests of its own besides the interests of the working class and the greatest possible majority of the people. Keeping this firmly in mind, we must steadfastly follow a distinctive Chinese path of anti-corruption and strengthen the Party Central Committee's centralized, unified leadership over anti-corruption work. While maintaining a tough stance against corruption, we should also strengthen checks on and oversight over the exercise of power, fortify the cultural-ethical foundations for championing integrity and disdaining corruption, and enhance coordinated efforts to prevent corruption by rooting out audacity, opportunity, and desire.
It was noted that strengthening Party regulations and institutions represents a long-term, fundamental strategy for ensuring full and rigorous Party self-governance. We must uphold the Party Constitution as the fundamental code of conduct for all Party members, deepen institutional reforms related to Party building, and integrate law-based governance of the country and regulation-based self-governance of the Party, thus providing strong institutional support for persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance. For this purpose, stronger measures will be taken to improve the framework of Party regulations and institutions, ensure the enforcement of institutions, and eliminate hidden rules.
It was stated that persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance entails further improvement to Party and state oversight systems. With this in mind, we should ensure that Party committees (leading Party members groups) exercise general oversight, improve the dual leadership system for discipline inspection and supervision, pursue greater integration and efficient collaboration between intraparty oversight and other avenues of oversight, and give play to the role of inspections as a powerful tool of comprehensive oversight.
It was stressed that persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance is the common political responsibility of all Party members. Attaching crucial importance to the responsibility system for Party self-supervision and self-governance, we will establish a robust, unified system where all sides perform their respective responsibilities in close collaboration. Furthermore, relevant performance assessment mechanisms will be improved, so that those who have failed to effectively carry out Party self-supervision and self-governance and caused serious problems in this regard are strictly held to account.
It was pointed out that studying and implementing the guiding principles from this plenary session represent a major political task for the entire Party both at present and in the period to come. With this in mind, we should fully grasp the guiding principles from the session, strengthen organization and leadership, and make tenacious efforts to solve prominent problems, seeing that all arrangements of the Resolution are implemented to the letter.
It was stressed that all aspects of our work agenda should be steadily advanced at the turn of the year. To fulfill this year's main goals and tasks for economic and social development and secure a good start for the 15th Five-Year Plan period, we will adhere to the general principle of pursuing progress while ensuring stability; fully and faithfully apply the new development philosophy on all fronts; move faster to foster a new pattern of development; make full and proper use of macro policies; tap deeper into the potential of domestic demand; further deepen reform and opening up; and pursue sustained and high-quality economic growth driven by innovation. In an effort to ensure security while pursuing development, we will press ahead with initiatives to see that public services are inclusive, meet essential needs, and provide a cushion for the people most in need, and deliver better results in our work related to workplace safety, disaster prevention, mitigation, and relief, food and drug safety, as well as social stability. As part of our endeavors to consolidate and expand the progress made in the study campaign on establishing and practicing the correct view of performance, we will, in the midst of a new round of elections at all levels, step up training for new members of leadership teams, particularly their heads, on the view of performance to inspire and guide them to deliver for the people through hard work in line with the requirements of serving the public good, benefiting the people, making sound decisions, and taking solid, down-to-earth actions.

The entire Party must unite and lead the Chinese people in forging ahead with one heart and one mind to achieve the goal of basically realizing socialist modernization and continue to break new ground in building a great country and advancing national rejuvenation on all fronts through Chinese modernization. With concrete actions, we will set the stage for the successful convening of this congress.

Iran's IRGC says 3 oil tankers hit mines in Strait of Hormuz
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
20:06:06 CST
21:06:06 KST

TEHRAN, Oct. 29 (Xinhua) -- The navy of Iran's Islamic Revolution Guard Corps (IRGC) announced on Thursday that three "violating" oil tankers that sought to cross the Strait of Hormuz through the "unauthorized" route south of the waterway exploded and caught fire after striking naval mines over the past 24 hours.
In a statement on the IRGC's official news outlet Sepah News, the navy said the vessels were abandoned off the strait's southern coasts.
It added the oil tankers had turned off all their radar and navigation systems and were trying to exit the strait through the "unauthorized" southern route in disregard of its warnings.
The IRGC Navy warned that the route has been mined and that vessel owners and crew will be responsible for the consequences of passage through it, stressing that they should not pay attention to U.S. Central Command's "delusions" on social media.
It underlined that reality will be determined on the ground, and that any provocative action taken with the "aggressive U.S. Army's support and malice," which disregards the regulations governing the strait, will be met with a decisive response.
Iran tightened its grip on the strait on Feb. 28, barring safe passage of vessels belonging to or affiliated with Israel and the United States following their joint strikes on Iranian territory.
In a separate statement on Thursday, the IRGC Navy said its electronic warfare unit managed within the preceding hours to take control of the guidance and navigation systems of a U.S. Army MQM-170 Outlaw "espionage and decoy" drone west of the strait and land it safely.
It added that the drone had been tasked with identifying Iran's air defense systems along the southern coasts, and data recovery showed it had taken off from the coast of a regional country.
In another statement on Thursday, the IRGC said its aerospace division's air defense systems shot down an MQ-1 Predator drone east of the strait within the preceding hour. It was the 14th MQ-1 intercepted by its air defense forces in recent months. ■

YANGON, Oct. 29 (Xinhua) -- Sunlight glints off the gilded spires of the Botahtaung Pagoda against a clear, pale blue sky in downtown Yangon. Tens of thousands of devotees have gathered here to pay homage to the Buddha during the Thadingyut Festival, one of Myanmar's most cherished occasions for family reunions and religious devotion.
On the full moon day of the festival, which marks the Buddha's descent from heaven, the pagoda compound hums with the footsteps of pilgrims and visitors.
"Since the Full Moon Day of Thadingyut coincides with my daughter's birthday, our family comes to the pagoda to perform meritorious deeds," said Ei Phyu, a local resident from Yangon.
During the three-day festival, which ran from Oct. 25 to 27 this year, her family lights oil lamps at home, makes donations, and prepares rice, meals and curries to offer to Buddhist monks and share with neighbours, she said on the sidelines of a candle-lighting event held by the pagoda's Board of Trustees on the evening of the full moon day.
Devotees like Ei Phyu are part of a vast wave of worshippers gathering at sacred landmarks across Myanmar. While Botahtaung Pagoda typically welcomes 4,000 to 5,000 visitors on a standard day, daily attendance leaps to between 30,000 and 70,000 during major religious holidays, according to U Aung Myat, a member of the pagoda's Board of Trustees.
The festive spirit extends far beyond Yangon, lighting up regions like Bagan and Kyaukse with hot-air balloon releases, live music concerts, and traditional contests.
In Kyaukse Town, located in the Mandalay Region, the famed Kyaukse Elephant Dance Competition stood out as a highlight of the weekend festivities.
U Tin Aung, who has served as a judge for the competition for over two decades, emphasized the heritage behind the spectacle. He noted that the 75-year-old tradition plays a vital role in preserving local cultural identity.
The Thadingyut Festival is a time for paying respect to elders and reuniting with family members who work in different places, he said, noting that the Kyaukse elephant dance festival also reflects these values, bringing people from towns and villages together in celebration.
Beyond offering ordinary citizens a welcome respite from daily hardships, the festival serves as a vital economic engine for local governments aiming to stimulate grassroots commerce and support small entrepreneurs.
In the ancient city of Bagan, market fairs showcasing traditional foods and products from micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) were held alongside traditional balloon releases in the pagoda-dense archaeological zone, according to U Myo Min Aung, deputy director of the Hotels and Tourism Development Implementation and Training Department in Bagan.
At People's Square in Yangon, Khin Thida Tun, owner of Pyae Thanakha, sold various value-added products made from thanakha, a natural cosmetic paste made from the ground bark, wood or roots of the thanakha tree, on the sidelines of a four-day Thadingyut fair featuring live performances and an MSME market fair.
"I'm thrilled to participate as an MSME owner because it gives us a chance to promote our brand locally and network with other businesses," she said, adding that her booth welcomed roughly 100 regular customers and new visitors in a single day. ■
