Ousted defense ministry chief to run for Parempoolsed at Riigikogu election
Kaimo Kuusk, former Defense Ministry permanent secretary and former ambassador to Ukraine, is joining Parempoolsed and running for the Riigikogu next spring.
Parempoolsed are seeking to win their first ever Riigikogu seats at the March 2027 election.
Kuusk said via a party press release that he decided to run because he wants to see real impact from his work for Estonia's benefit: "I want my experience, skills and values to serve Estonia's security and defense capability."
He also hit out at what he called undemocratic approaches taken by some of the major parties.
"I can't stand by and watch Estonian democracy being eroded. It's very important to me that Estonia be a state governed by law. I won't accept it if Reform runs the same kind of politics in the country as Center does in Tallinn, where positions aren't allocated via competitions but in the party office," Kuusk said.
Kuusk also criticized the government's decision to hold a planned Ukraine aid conference in late January, which he said, given the situation there in winter, is the least suitable time for Ukraine yet convenient for campaign point-scoring for some of the political parties.
"We're setting the Ukraine reconstruction conference at the least suitable time for the Ukrainians, as Reform and Eesti 200 politicians want to tie it to the front of their election cart. Aid to Ukraine like this is of no benefit to Ukraine," Kuusk added. He noted a worrying trend which he says has emerged in Estonian politics whereby aid to Ukraine is seen primarily as having election propaganda value, at the cost of the state's functioning. "Various state institutions have consequently fallen out with each other. Something has gone wrong when, during a war, the most important question becomes who gets to open a kindergarten in Ukraine."
Kuusk stressed he joined Parempoolsed, founded shortly before the last Riigikogu elections in 2023, as he believes in the party's team and clear plans. "Parempoolsed offer values-based politics that will make Estonia's future better. I like that Parempoolsed dare to decide," he explained.
Parempoolsed chair Lavly Perling said she values Kuusk as a team player. "In addition, Kaimo hasn't worked on aiding Ukraine only on paper, but has been physically on the ground in Ukraine. I also know that as ambassador Kaimo was very active in economic diplomacy, opening doors in Ukraine for Estonian companies," said Perling, a former prosecutor general who has worked in Ukraine.
"Kaimo joining the team makes us even stronger and shows that people believe in Parempoolsed. For the voter who wants a better future for Estonia, the only alternative to the populists in spring 2027 is Parempoolsed," Perling added.
Kuusk, 50, was Estonia's ambassador to Ukraine from 2019 to 2023, ambassador to Lithuania from 2023 to 2024, and Defense Ministry permanent secretary from 2024 until September. Before entering the foreign service he worked for several decades at the Foreign Intelligence Service (Välisluureamet).
Kuusk was dismissed as Defense Ministry permanent secretary in September, weeks after incoming Defense Minister Martin Herem (Reform) made Kuusk's departure a condition of taking up the ministerial spot.
Kuusk's last working day at the ministry was September 15. The government justified his dismissal on the basis of failed cooperation. SDE chair Lauri Läänemets asked the Chancellor of Justice to review the legality of that dismissal. Hanno Pevkur, who resigned as defense minister at the start of September following a defense procurement scandal, said national defense leadership could not be left the victim of mutual distrust.

ATESH reported sabotage at a substation supplying electricity to a missile fuel plant in Russia
Kyiv • UNN
ATESH reported damage to the electrical equipment of a substation supplying the Kamensky Combine in the Rostov region. There is no independent confirmation of the consequences.
Agents of the "Atesh" partisan movement said they had disabled the electrical equipment of a substation in the city of Kamensk-Shakhtinsky, Rostov region, Russia. The facility supplies electricity to an enterprise that produces solid rocket fuel for Russian weapons. The "Atesh" movement reported this, UNN writes.
Details
According to the partisans, during the act of sabotage, the switchgear cabinet of the electrical substation supplying the federal state-owned enterprise "Kamensky Combine" was damaged.
This plant belongs to Russia's military-industrial complex and specializes in producing solid rocket fuel for the "Uragan," "Smerch," and "Tornado-S" multiple-launch rocket systems, as well as other missile and aviation systems.
The act of sabotage may have caused disruptions in rocket fuel production
The "Atesh" movement claims that the damage to the distribution equipment has created problems with the enterprise's power supply and requires repair work.
According to the partisans, such incidents disrupt production processes, as plant workers are forced to focus on restoring the equipment instead of carrying out their primary production tasks.
The movement emphasized that targeted acts of sabotage in Russia's rear are aimed at complicating the operations of enterprises that meet the needs of the Russian army.
The partisans also said they continue to identify vulnerabilities in Russia's rear infrastructure and conduct operations against facilities involved in military production.
There is currently no independent confirmation of the extent of the damage to the electrical substation or the possible consequences for the combine's operations.

14:25:10 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — Taichung-based AerosoarX Chair Max Lo (羅正方) said Wednesday that the firm signed cooperation memorandums with US companies Rajant and SiMa.ai to develop AI-enabled drones and support local assembly in overseas markets, CNA reported.
Lo, who previously founded Tainan’s Geosat Aerospace, established AerosoarX on April 17. The company showcased a 15-inch foldable drone developed for the US Department of Defense’s Drone Dominance Program at the signing event.
Lo said the Russia-Ukraine war offered important lessons. He added that individual firms could no longer provide all-in-one solutions and should instead form strategic alliances with partners in like-minded countries to speed up development.
Lo said AerosoarX produces about 70% of its components in Taiwan and ships partially assembled drone platforms for final assembly at locations such as Rajant’s plant in Kentucky. He said this approach is more efficient and helps reduce tariff costs.
The company said the partnership combines its drone platforms with Rajant’s communications technology and SiMa.ai’s onboard AI capabilities. The three firms are targeting the Indo-Pacific, Europe, the US, and Japan.
AerosoarX works with Rajant on US military projects, supplying drone subsystems and components. Shipments began in April and May, with assembly and integration expected to be completed in November.
For Japan’s interceptor drone requirements, AerosoarX is helping replace Chinese-made components with alternatives from other countries.
Lo said Ukraine, Poland, and the Czech Republic are proving grounds for drone technologies. AerosoarX is shipping key components and systems to the front lines to ensure they meet operational requirements.
AerosoarX plans to set up production across the first island chain. It aims to ensure supply chain stability, local control over production, and a division of labor among partners.
Regarding the US Department of Defense’s Drone Dominance Program, Lo said AerosoarX had delivered nearly 1,000 drones to the US. He said shipments could reach 10,000 units if the company successfully passes the program’s third-stage evaluation in 2027.

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — DPP Taipei mayoral candidate Puma Shen (沈伯洋) leads incumbent Taipei Mayor Chiang Wan-an (蔣萬安) by 4 percentage points in voter support, according to a UDN poll.
The survey found that 45% of respondents supported Shen, compared with 41% for Chiang, a gap within the poll's margin of error. However, 48% expected Chiang to win reelection, while 35% predicted a victory for Shen, with 30 days remaining before the Nov. 28 local elections.
The poll found that 79% of Taipei voters were following the mayoral race, with 91% of Shen's supporters interested in the election, compared with 77% of Chiang's supporters. Meanwhile, 79% of respondents said life in Taipei was generally going well, and half approved of Chiang's performance as mayor, while 37% disapproved and 13% had no opinion.
Shen had stronger support among women and younger voters, while Chiang performed better among older age groups. Among men, 45% supported Chiang and 43% backed Shen, while Shen led Chiang by 9 percentage points among women, with 47% support.
Among voters younger than 40, Shen received 58% support, leading Chiang by 25 percentage points. Chiang led Shen by 1 percentage point among voters aged 40 to 59, with 44% support, and by 6 points among those aged 60 and older.
Among DPP supporters, 91% backed Shen, while 86% of KMT supporters backed Chiang. Among TPP supporters, 75% favored Chiang and 16% supported Shen. Among independent voters, 40% backed Shen, 33% supported Chiang, and 26% remained undecided.
On public image, 46% viewed Shen favorably and 31% unfavorably, compared with 44% and 36% for Chiang. On trustworthiness regarding major policies and personal pledges, 40% considered Chiang more consistent and trustworthy, while 39% trusted Shen more and 21% had no opinion.
Shen also led in voter perceptions of the candidates' visions for Taipei, with 44% finding his proposals more appealing, compared with 28% who favored Chiang's vision. Among voters younger than 40, nearly 60% preferred Shen's vision.
The poll was conducted Oct. 20-22 and Oct. 25, interviewing 1,115 adults registered as Taipei residents, while 264 people declined to participate. The survey had a margin of error of plus or minus 3 percentage points at a 95% confidence level.

Anthropic warns Taiwan conflict could disrupt global AI chip supply
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
05:24:44 UTC
14:24:44 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — Anthropic has warned that a military conflict, blockade, or natural disaster affecting Taiwan could severely disrupt global supplies of advanced chips for years.
The AI company filed for an IPO with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on Monday. Its filing identifies Taiwan’s dominance in advanced semiconductor manufacturing as a risk to its ability to secure the chips needed to develop and operate its AI systems.
Anthropic said the majority of the world’s most advanced chipmaking capacity is concentrated in Taiwan, primarily at TSMC. It warned that “any military conflict, tariffs and trade restrictions, economic coercion, blockade, natural disaster, or other incident affecting Taiwan could severely disrupt the global supply of advanced chips, with effects that could persist for years.”
The company said the nation’s concentration of advanced chip production exposes the global supply chain to earthquakes, typhoons, geopolitical tensions between Taiwan and China, and disruptions to the power grid, water supply, and other critical infrastructure. Efforts to expand advanced chipmaking capacity outside Taiwan, including in the US, remain in the early stages and may not materially reduce risks in the foreseeable future, it said.
Anthropic also disclosed that TSMC has sometimes been unable to meet market demand for chip manufacturing capacity. As a result, the company said it has “not always been able to obtain sufficient quantities of chips on a timely basis.”
The filing said any restrictions or delays affecting advanced chip supplies from Taiwan or TSMC could adversely affect Anthropic’s business, financial condition, and operating results.

US Army Pacific readying for potential Chinese invasion of Taiwan next year
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
04:29:56 UTC
13:29:56 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — The US Army Pacific has made preparations for a Chinese invasion of Taiwan next year, its commander, General Ronald Clark, said Tuesday.
The threat posed by the Davidson window is “still valid,” Clark said during the TechNet Indo-Pacific conference in Honolulu, Stars and Stripes reported. The Davidson window refers to then-US Indo-Pacific Command chief Admiral Philip Davidson’s assessment in 2021 that China would have the military capability to invade Taiwan by 2027.
However, an annual Office of the Director of National Intelligence report said the threat to Taiwan was not imminent, per Stars and Stripes. “Chinese leaders do not currently plan to execute an invasion of Taiwan in 2027, nor do they have a fixed timeline for achieving unification,” the report said.
Clark described the Davidson window as “a period of time for which we’re snapping the chalk line to say we need to be ready by this date.” “So, we’ve embarked upon a strategic approach to setting the theater that we refer to as ‘Army Ready Forward’,” he said.
Under this plan, Army Pacific has rotated troops, equipment, and supplies through islands west of the International Date Line, closer to China, Clark said.
The biggest challenge is balancing “exquisite high-end systems and affordable, mass-producible alternatives,” especially for autonomous systems, he said.

Australia is considering purchasing missile interceptors developed for Israel's Iron Dome as it seeks to rapidly build an air defence shield, officials said on Thursday.
Citing rapid changes in warfare seen in Ukraine and the Middle East, defence officials told a parliamentary committee that Australia wanted to have a ground-based missile defence system by the "early 2030s".

Australia does not supply weapons to Israel and its purchase of Israeli defence products has come under political scrutiny.

Evolving Scope of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
04:21:00 UTC
13:21:00 KST

On October 25, Pakistan’s Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar met Chinese Ambassador Jiang Zaidong in Islamabad to review progress on the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC).
According to a statement issued by Pakistan’s Foreign Office, the discussions centered on advancing trade, investment, regional connectivity, agricultural modernization, and people-to-people exchanges. Dar also stressed the need for sustained high-level engagements to advance what the Pakistani officials describe as a “Pakistan-China Community of Shared Future in the New Era.” The meeting comes as both countries seek to fast-track the second phase of CPEC.
It appears to be part of the two countries’ ongoing effort to accelerate CPEC-related work and clarify the project’s second phase.
Phase one of the project is known for largely delivering energy projects, roads, and basic connectivity infrastructure. Phase two, on the other hand, is expected to emphasize industrial cooperation, mining, critical minerals, agriculture, and technology. Moreover, information sharing and people-to-people exchanges, long described as pillars of the corridor’s long-term vision, along with opening the mineral sector, are increasingly framed as part of the second phase.
On the ground, the path being taken to accelerate the second phase already looks different from the large-scale infrastructure focus that defined the early years of development.
Pakistan and China recently launched the China-Pakistan Information Corridor (CPIC), to counter what officials have called “misleading narratives,” expand cultural exchanges, and strengthen think tank cooperation.
From the Pakistani and Chinese perspectives, such narratives have often portrayed CPEC as little more than a debt burden or a strategic liability rather than a development partnership. The new information corridor, it seems, is intended to present a more coordinated account of the relationship. Moreover, a closer think tank engagement could, in principle, help policymakers in both countries better align priorities and reduce the informational friction that has occasionally complicated implementation. In that sense, CPIC seems linked to the practical needs of CPEC rather than standing apart from them.
In his address to inaugurate CPIC, Pakistan’s Information Minister Ataullah Tarar captured the intended shift when he observed that the first phase of CPEC connected lands, while the next would “connect our minds.” He said the information corridor will act as a bridge between the peoples of the two countries.
Arguably, this renewed emphasis on information sharing and narrative alignment is based on the fact that public perceptions and policy coordination matter as much as physical infrastructure at this stage.
Whether the issue of misinformation has undermined cooperation in the past remains open to debate. However, the decision to institutionalize fact-checking mechanisms and joint media working groups suggests that both countries now treat the issue as one that needs addressing now rather than deferred as a secondary concern.
Pakistan and China are also focusing on mapping, regulating, and opening Pakistan’s mineral sector, particularly in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) province. CPEC’s phase two is expected to prioritize industrial cooperation, mining, and the excavation of critical minerals as well. Special economic zones, which are being set up, are more likely to succeed if the industries located in them can process local resources rather than simply assemble or package imported inputs.
In this regard, Rashakai Special Economic Zone (RSEZ) in KP offers a useful illustration of such cooperation between Pakistan and China. The project is operated through a joint venture involving the China Road and Bridge Corporation (CRBC) and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Economic Zone and Management Company. The SEZ was designed from the outset around value-addition industries, with mineral processing listed among its core designated sectors.
Provincial authorities in KP have recently intensified this message, particularly on mineral extraction and refining in the province. KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi recently said that the province’s mineral resources would be extracted and sold to promote economic prosperity. He urged foreign companies to invest through joint ventures.
The timing of Kundi’s statement is particularly notable. The renewed emphasis on mineral governance comes amid a recent provincial leadership change in KP following the imposition of governor’s rule, which has shifted administrative authority from the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI)-led provincial government to the federal government. Under this arrangement, Islamabad could now exercise more influence over provincial regulatory affairs, including strategic mineral assets.
This administrative shift has temporarily softened long-standing frictions between the federal and provincial governments over resource management and joint investment frameworks.
These developments point to a CPEC phase that appears to be less about infrastructure and more about information coordination, industrial networks, and the organized development of Pakistan’s mineral base.
Similarly, the approach of Pakistan and China in the second phase is different from the first phase as it appears to rest on the idea that closer policy alignment and people-to-people understanding will make the economic partnership under CPEC more viable over the long run.

New Zealand construction costs steady despite sharp rise in diesel prices

12:13:40 CST
13:13:40 KST

WELLINGTON, Oct. 29 (Xinhua) -- New Zealand construction costs remained relatively steady in October despite a sharp rise in diesel prices, with average construction trade rates increasing just 0.1 percent over the past month, industry data showed on Thursday.
Diesel prices rose an average of 19 percent from the previous month and were 76.2 percent higher than in February. Fuel-intensive construction activities saw more noticeable increases, with excavation costs rising 3.9 percent, while piling and demolition costs both increased 0.6 percent, according to the latest Quotable Value (QV) CostBuilder monthly construction cost update.
The update recorded more than 7,000 data changes across major New Zealand cities including Auckland, Wellington, Christchurch, Dunedin, Hamilton and Palmerston North.
Other price rises included processed timber products, up 6.2 percent, medium-density fiberboard, up 2.8 percent, reinforcing, up 2.7 percent, and roofing and cladding, up 1.6 percent, it showed.
However, some costs declined, including adhesives and sealants, down 4.2 percent, kitchen-related costs, down 1.2 percent, and structural timber, down 0.2 percent, statistics showed.
Rising fuel costs had not translated into broad-based construction cost inflation, as increases and decreases across different products and trades largely offset each other, QV CostBuilder quantity surveyor Martin Bisset said in a statement.
Bisset advised those budgeting for construction work to continue allowing for cost fluctuations, particularly in fuel-sensitive areas. ■

Regulators say latest Fukushima discharge will not affect Taiwan

02:43:49 UTC
11:43:49 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — The latest round of treated wastewater discharge from Japan’s Fukushima Daiichi nuclear plant will have no impact on Taiwan, the Nuclear Safety Commission said Tuesday.
In a press release, the NSC said the plant began releasing a new batch of wastewater on Monday, scheduled to run for 19 days. Japan began discharging treated wastewater containing tritium from the tsunami-disabled plant in August 2023.
Japan’s treatment process reduces most radionuclides in the wastewater to below regulatory limits, but tritium cannot be filtered out and is instead diluted with seawater before discharge, according to Japan’s Ministry of Economy, Trade, and Industry.
The NSC said that tritium levels in waters around Taiwan are forecast to “remain below the minimum detectable level of monitoring instruments,” citing Central Weather Administration forecasts. Based on analysis by the Tokyo Electric Power Company, levels of radionuclides other than tritium also met regulatory standards.
The commission added that the recently discharged wastewater is expected to affect mainly waters off Japan’s east coast due to tidal movements.
The NSC monitors seawater radiation in cooperation with other government agencies, and it said that no abnormalities so far have been detected.
Real-time updates on how the wastewater is dispersing is available on the CWA’s website.

Matthias Schmale, the UN Resident and Humanitarian Coordinator in Ukraine, announced the plan at an event on the UN’s response to the humanitarian crisis caused by Russia’s war against Ukraine, Ukrinform reports, citing its correspondent.
“We plan to provide assistance to 2.1 million people from October 26, 2026, through March 2027. by Sportswriters Li Chunyu, Li Bowen
BEIJING, Oct. 29 (Xinhua) -- As 16-year-old home prodigy Sun Xinran clinched the women's singles title at the ITF World Tennis Tour Junior Finals in Chengdu on Sunday, Chinese tennis embraced another highlight this autumn besides the ATP and WTA tournaments in the China Swing.
Running through September to November, the China Swing covers cities including Beijing, Shanghai, Wuhan, Chengdu, Hangzhou, Ningbo, Guangzhou and Hong Kong. The 2025 edition drew nearly one million on-site spectators, generating about 250 million yuan (37.5 million U.S. dollars) in ticket revenue and driving over 2.4 billion dollars in related consumption, according to the Tennis Administration Center.
The Tennis Administration Center had already moved to sustain that momentum, issuing reform measures in 2025 covering event supply, talent development and public participation. This September, ahead of the National Day holiday, the General Office of the State Council issued guidelines on unleashing the potential of sports consumption, explicitly supporting high-level professional events such as tennis.
The policy push and the season's momentum have met this autumn. The China Swing has become a window into China's tennis industry and sports-event consumption: from "second-screen" viewing areas to ticket-stub economies, from wild cards tilted toward young Chinese players to a public picking up rackets.
BREAKTHROUGHS AT HOME
Zheng Qinwen's triumph at the China Open was one of the most remarkable moments. The Olympic champion claimed her maiden WTA 1000 title to become the first Chinese player to win the tournament's women's singles crown.
"To play in China is like the fifth Grand Slam for me. I want to perform super well in front of my people," said Zheng, who celebrated her 24th birthday during the China Open in Beijing. "Coming back from the elbow injury, I find my inner fire back and want to be a more aggressive player."
Zheng was not the only Chinese player to benefit from home tournaments. Wild card Sun reached the women's singles last 32 at the China Open, where she faced opponents of rising rank with each round.
"This tournament gave me opportunity to play against top players. From the first round to the third round, my opponents are getting higher in their rankings. This really motivates me to improve myself," said Sun, who took the girls' singles title at this year's US Open.
At the Wuhan Open, qualifier Shi Han upset Alexandra Eala of the Philippines for her first WTA 1000 main-draw win.
Bai Xilin, director of China's Tennis Administration Center, noted that the China Swing provides more opportunities for home players with wild cards and qualifying matches.
"It serves to unleash the potential of our domestic players and inspire their growth in a long run through high-level events," Bai said.
For overseas athletes, the China Swing offers a chance to explore the host cities. Novak Djokovic took the Summer Palace as a favorite destination.
"I respect Chinese culture and tradition very much. Actually I was staying in a hotel that is just next to the Summer Palace. I've been going there every day. No joke. It's a stunning place more than just nature," said the 39-year-old Djokovic, who claimed his seventh China Open men's singles title this year.
"Tennis brings together players and fans from different countries and backgrounds. Through the tournament coverage and the players' own social channels, international audiences can also discover more aspects of China," said Fabrice Chouquet, a WTA senior official.
ECONOMIC ACES
For Vietnamese businessman Dang Phu, his destination in China has always been the Canton Fair in autumn. But this year, he and colleagues arrived earlier than usual to watch the Wuhan Open and then the Shanghai Masters.
"We wanted to see top players compete in person and experience the atmosphere," Dang said.
"People came to watch the match not only for the competition itself, but to feel the urban life. So, the organizers need to focus more on how an event can draw larger crowds and channel these visitors into a full range of consumption scenarios across the host city," said Huang Haiyan, a professor at Beijing Sport University.
According to the China Open organizing committee, total consumption during the tournament is projected to exceed 8.2 million dollars, up 55 percent year-on-year, with licensed product revenue doubling to 4.2 million dollars. Over 450,000 visitors entered the National Tennis Center, up 25 percent, including around 60 percent from other cities and nearly 10,000 international spectators.
Even though the Wuhan Open was not scheduled for the National Day holiday this year and home favorite Zheng was absent through injury, the tournament still drew 202,700 on-site spectators, 48 percent of whom traveled from other cities.
"The tournament not only drives direct spending on tickets, licensed products and catering services, but also spurs consumption on accommodation, transport and tourism," said Hong Xuyan, deputy director of the Wuhan Sports Bureau.
At the Shanghai Masters, around 248,000 on-site spectators watched the tournament, two thirds from outside Shanghai. "The total revenue reached 75 million dollars, with sponsorship contributing roughly 50 percent and ticketing for 20 percent," said Yang Yibin, chairman of Shanghai Juss Sports Development Group.
"Tennis fans feature high per-capita spending. They stay longer and always follow a complete consumption chain spanning tickets, catering, accommodation and tourism for multiplier effect," noted Wang Xueli, a professor at Tsinghua University's School of Economics and Management.
The broader industry is growing too. China's tennis industry was worth 5.5 billion dollars in 2024, up 15 percent year-on-year, according to the Tennis Administration Center.
NURTURING TENNIS CULTURE
Chinese tennis player Ji Mianyi, 20, sensed the tennis boom through her family and friends.
"When the topic turns to sports, they used to think of table tennis or badminton first. But after Zheng won the women's singles gold at the Paris 2024 Olympic Games, more people around me wanted to learn from scratch and asked me how long it takes to be able to compete," Ji said.
Her observations are borne out by the data. China's tennis population reached 25.19 million in 2024, up 28.03 percent from 19.67 million in 2021 and about a quarter of the global total, according to the Tennis Administration Center. The number of courts rose from 49,767 to 53,805 over the same period, up 8.12 percent.
Two decades ago, when Zheng Jie and Yan Zi claimed China's first women's doubles Grand Slam title at the 2006 Australian Open, tennis still seemed far from most Chinese people. The country had nearly two million participants and about 10,000 courts, according to figures from that year.
"There were much fewer youth tennis tournaments in China at that time," Zheng Jie recalled. "Then, the outstanding performance of Chinese players, including Li Na and Zheng Qinwen, kept stoking public enthusiasm for tennis."
By 2025, Guangdong, Sichuan, Hubei, Beijing and Zhejiang are the top five regions by tennis population, all hosting ATP or WTA tournaments as part of the China Swing. Only 5,402 youth players are registered with the General Administration of Sport, but roughly 506,000 young players have competition records outside the registered system, according to the Tennis Administration Center.
Shanghai, home to the Masters, has maintained strong momentum. At the PMAX Tennis Center, its 12 courts have become a thriving hub.
"Our tennis center hosts training courses and tournaments, catering to enthusiasts of different stages," introduced Jia Jingzhe, one of the center's partners. "Powered by this model, the center's monthly revenue has been around 200,000 dollars since March this year, more than quadrupling over four years compared with 2022."
Among the customers at PMAX, adults account for more than 60 percent, with women in the majority. According to the Shanghai Tennis Association, the city's tennis-playing population reached 980,000 in 2025, and more than 30 newly opened venues added over 100 standard courts.
"Tennis is an integral part of my life," said enthusiast Zhu Lingjun, who plays three to four hours every week and uses AI to review her game.
From professional tournaments to grassroots courts, tennis has been evolving into a lifestyle in China.
"International studies have found that long-term tennis participation can help extend people's lifespan by improving sleep and modulating nervous system," Bai said. "Our goal is to ensure that tennis is accessible to everyone, and we are striving toward that vision." ■

5 Things to Consider When Planning Interior Thresholds
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
01:30:00 UTC
10:30:00 KST

An opening between two rooms shapes how people move through a building, what they see from one space to another, and whether an area feels connected or separate. Although doors are among the most frequently used interior architectural elements, their impact on the interior organization is often considered late in the design process. Yet their movement and relationship to surrounding surfaces influence circulation, furniture placement, and the perception of space.
In residential renovations, these decisions are particularly important. Existing walls, structural elements, building services, and ceiling heights can limit options, while new layouts often balance open-plan living with the need for privacy. In new construction, architects have greater freedom to coordinate wall cavities, suspended ceilings, and door mechanisms from the outset.
The question is how two spaces should relate: remain connected, be separated, or alternate between the two? Openings, partitions, hinged doors, pivot doors, sliding doors, and furniture each offer different possibilities. Door systems such as those developed by ECLISSE provide different approaches to these transitions, responding to existing construction conditions and the intended spatial arrangement.
1. Defining the Relationship Between Spaces
A kitchen connected to a living room may benefit from a wide opening that preserves visual continuity while still allowing separation during cooking or entertaining. A home office may stay open during the day but still need visual and acoustic privacy for focused work or calls. In both cases, the design must balance openness with the option of separation.
Not every transition requires a door. Changes in floor finish, deeper openings, screens, or variations in ceiling height can distinguish areas without closing them off. Furniture can serve a similar purpose: a kitchen island, freestanding storage unit, or shelving system can define zones, guide circulation, and provide storage without creating a full-height partition.
2. Choosing a Door System
The door mechanism affects circulation and usable space. Hinged doors require clearance for their swing, which must be coordinated with furniture, corridors, and adjacent doors. Pivot doors let larger panels rotate around pivot points set away from a conventional side hinge.
Sliding doors move parallel to a wall or partition, avoiding the floor space a swinging panel requires. Ceiling-, surface-mounted, and integrated sliding door systems such as the ECLISSE Exo and Endo leave the panel visible when open, while pocket doors slide into a cavity within the wall. The latter leave the opening unobstructed and free up the adjacent wall surface, but require sufficient space within the partition and coordination with electrical installations and other services.
The distinction becomes particularly relevant in renovations. A ceiling- or surface-mounted track can be installed without creating a door cavity within the wall or requiring a suspended ceiling, which can simplify projects where existing construction must remain in place. A ceiling-integrated sliding door and pocket door may be easier to accommodate in a new partition designed around the mechanism. The decision depends on available construction depth, the intended opening, and the functions the surrounding wall must support.
3. Visible or Concealed
For sliding doors, the sliding mechanism is part of the architectural detail. Its position affects the ceiling, wall finish, and the opening's appearance when the panel is open or closed. Choosing between a visible track and a recessed system also influences how the door relates to surrounding surfaces.
In a ceiling- or surface-mounted sliding door system, such as the ECLISSE Exo, a track support is mounted on the wall or ceiling and concealed behind a 65-mm-high aluminum pelmet. Its appearance can coordinate with the surrounding surfaces or remain a visible architectural detail, available in finishes such as white, black, or a paintable primer.
A ceiling-integrated sliding door system, such as ECLISSE Endo, integrates the track support into a suspended ceiling. Once finished, the support sits flush with the ceiling, leaving only a slim slot for the visible sliding guide. The primer-coated surface can be painted to match the ceiling, allowing the mechanism to recede visually. The system can be installed in front of or inside the passageway, ideal for large openings. This approach requires the ceiling construction to accommodate the recessed support; however, it is adjustable and can accommodate unevenness in the ceiling slab. Both systems accommodate wooden panels and glass panels with aluminum frames. Individual panels can measure up to 1,300 mm wide and 3 m high, with a specified thickness of 40 mm.
4. Configuring Openings
The passage width affects the number of panels and the space needed for their movement. A single panel may suit a standard doorway, while wider openings can use two opposing panels that meet in the center. Multiple tracks accommodate several panels, and fixed panels can extend the overall glazed or opaque surface.
Sliding door systems, such as ECLISSE Exo and Endo, are available in single-, double-, and triple-track configurations. Both also allow two opposing panels on the same track, with fixed panels as an additional option. These arrangements can accommodate wider connections between living areas, kitchens, and multipurpose rooms. The open position requires as much consideration as the closed one. Available wall or ceiling length, where panels collect, and the position of switches and furniture all affect how much of the passage remains clear.
5. The Door as Part of the Interior
Material choices also affect the relationship between spaces. A door's finish influences how the threshold reads within a room. A panel matching the wall color can reduce visual interruptions, while contrasting timber, glass, or a dark track can emphasize the opening. Glass maintains visual continuity, while an opaque panel provides greater visual separation. A sliding panel can close off an area when needed and leave the layout open when retracted. Flush-to-wall doors offer another way to maintain continuity by aligning the door leaf with the surrounding wall.
The aim is not to make every boundary disappear, but to determine where it should remain visible, where it should recede, and how it should respond to everyday use. Coordinating the opening, panel movement, supporting structure, and finish allows doors to become part of the spatial plan.

US Justice Department loses initial bid to block votes from alleged non-citizens in California
- A US judge blocked the Justice Department’s bid to stop California counting mail ballots from more than 20,000 voters flagged as likely non-citizens.
- Judge David Carter said the request broke constitutional rules and warned it could cause chaos, erode trust, and wrongly strip voters of their rights.
- The Justice Department appealed, while California said its safeguards are strong and the federal claims rely on “suspect data”; similar moves were also made in Alaska and Washington.
AI generated
LOS ANGELES – A US judge strongly rebuked the Trump administration on Oct 28 by rejecting a request by the Justice Department to temporarily block California from counting any mail ballots for the midterm elections from more than 20,000 registered voters the department alleges are likely non-citizens.
The decision marks the latest setback for President Donald Trump’s effort to boost the federal government’s role in elections ahead of the Nov 3 midterms, with his Republican Party locked in a tight battle to retain control of both houses of Congress.
US District Judge David Carter issued the decision after a hearing on Oct 27 in Los Angeles federal court over the Justice Department’s request for a temporary restraining order barring officials from counting any ballots from the individuals it flagged.
The Justice Department’s lawsuit, filed on Oct 15, was a rare intervention in the voting process weeks before an election and signalled the Trump administration’s willingness to contest the midterm results in court.
“Never before in American history has the federal government, on the eve of an election, sought to coerce a state and local government to abandon its own constitutional election procedures and bend to the will of the executive branch,” Carter wrote on Oct 28.
The judge, an appointee of then Democratic President Bill Clinton, said the Justice Department’s last-minute request to exclude more than 20,000 ballots ran afoul of “longstanding constitutional principles mandating that states have control over their elections”.
Carter warned that a ruling in the Trump administration’s favour could create chaos and cause thousands of registered voters to “potentially lose the right that generations of Americans have fought to preserve”.
“Eroded trust in our democracy is irreparable,” Carter wrote. “Once a vote is segregated, lasting harm has occurred. If the executive (branch) can discount votes and threaten an ongoing election due to unproven allegations, then our democracy is in danger.”
The Justice Department swiftly appealed the decision to the 9th US Circuit Court of Appeals.
“Every day, more ballots are processed by election officials,” Justice Department lawyer Bill Essayli said in a statement.
“This ongoing emergency disenfranchises American citizens through dilution.”
California has said the state’s safeguards against non-citizen voting are robust. It said the Justice Department’s assertions relied on “suspect data” and that complying with its demands would risk disenfranchising eligible voters.
California is the most populous US state and a Democratic stronghold. It has more seats in the House of Representatives – 52 – than any other state.
Trump has made California a focal point of his sweeping immigration crackdown since returning to the White House, accusing it of undermining public safety through its “sanctuary state” policies that limit cooperation with federal immigration enforcement.
Trump has repeatedly insisted that states are not doing enough to stop voting by non-citizens, which he says is widespread despite multiple studies and state audits showing it is rare.
Appeals court rejected emergency request
The hearing comes after a federal appeals court on Oct 26 rejected an unusual emergency request by the Justice Department asking the appeals court to temporarily block California from counting the ballots before Carter had the chance to rule.
The Justice Department did not indicate how many of the more than 20,000 people it flagged in California had actually submitted a mail ballot.
It had argued that a restraining order was necessary to ensure that California did not impede prosecutors’ ability to enforce a federal law that makes it illegal for non-citizens to vote in federal elections.
But Carter said the Justice Department never explained why counting ballots would impair any prosecutions under the law, as states are not required to help the federal government investigate and prosecute crimes.
Apart from California, the Trump administration has sought to intervene in elections in two states that are home to competitive races.
In Alaska, the Justice Department last week asked a judge to prevent certification of election results if the Republican incumbent senator loses by a slim margin, alleging that the presence of another candidate with a similar name on the ballot could confuse voters.
Alaska has urged that the case be dismissed, arguing it has taken steps to distinguish the two candidates on the ballot.
In Washington state, the Justice Department on Oct 26 sent a letter asking officials not to count any ballots received from 400 voters it said may not be citizens.
Washington’s top election official said the timing of the request indicated it was intended to cast unfounded suspicion on election results.
California had 23 million registered voters as at December 2025, while Washington had five million registered voters as at 2024, state records show.
Voting rights activists have expressed concern that the federal government’s methods for scrutinising state voter lists to identify non-citizen voters risk wrongly flagging naturalised citizens for removal from the rolls. REUTERS

US hospitals and nursing homes are breeding grounds for deadly superbugs – CDC
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
00:45:34 UTC
09:45:34 KST

US hospitals and nursing homes are breeding grounds for deadly superbugs – CDC
More than four in five US deaths linked to drug-resistant infections involve pathogens commonly associated with hospitals and nursing homes, according to a new report from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).
The agency’s Antimicrobial Resistance Threats Report released this week draws on data from 2023 and estimates that 19 types of drug-resistant bacteria and fungi cause 9.7 million infections and 50,800 deaths annually in the US. Seven bacterial threats commonly associated with hospitals and nursing homes accounted for more than 42,000 of those deaths, along with nearly $12 billion in healthcare costs.
Antimicrobial resistance occurs when germs develop the ability to withstand drugs designed to kill them, making infections difficult or impossible to treat. Elderly people, those with weakened immune systems, and patients undergoing invasive medical procedures are particularly vulnerable.
Among the pathogens classified as urgent threats is Candida auris, a potentially deadly fungus that can resist multiple medications and survive on surfaces in healthcare facilities. It primarily affects seriously ill patients and can cause dangerous bloodstream infections.
A separate CDC study published in July found that reported cases of Candida auris more than doubled from 2022-2024, rising from 2,882 to 6,197. Most cases for which the type of medical facility was identified were detected in hospitals, including those that provide long-term treatment for seriously ill patients.
The CDC noted that many healthcare-associated infections are preventable, but much of the progress in combating drug resistance was lost during the Covid-19 pandemic, when staffing shortages, overcrowding, and disruptions to infection-control practices contributed to a rise in infections.
The warning comes as US hospitals face mounting financial and staffing pressures. A Harvard-led study published earlier this month found that 432 hospitals closed nationwide from 2010-2025, resulting in a net loss of 216 facilities and more than 24,000 beds.
Nursing homes are also struggling with bed and staffing shortages. An investigation in September by KFF Health News found that declining capacity forced some patients to remain hospitalized longer because suitable care facilities were unavailable.

Pakistan makes U-turn on Taiwan airline ban – media
Pakistan has restored overflight rights to two Taiwanese airlines after they stopped using its airspace three days earlier, according to AP, Bloomberg, and Dawn.
On Wednesday, Islamabad issued permits allowing Taiwan-based China Airlines and EVA Air to use Pakistani airspace until March 27, 2027, the outlets reported, citing official documents.
Hours earlier, Pakistani Defense Minister Khawaja Asif defended restrictions on Taiwanese carriers, citing Islamabad’s longstanding adherence to Beijing’s One-China policy.
“The aviation division follows the One-China policy – only mainland China is allowed,” Asif told Bloomberg. “We have permitted only Chinese airlines to fly over Pakistan.”
According to flight-tracking data, Taiwanese airlines began rerouting flights to avoid Pakistani airspace on October 25. Taipei condemned Islamabad for what it described as undermining Taiwan’s sovereignty and “politicizing and weaponizing airspace,” according to Taiwanese media.
Most countries, including the US and Russia, do not formally recognize Taiwan as an independent state. Beijing considers the self-governing island part of China and seeks reunification, preferably through peaceful means, but has not ruled out the use of force. Washington and several other Western governments maintain unofficial ties with Taiwan and supply it with weapons, drawing condemnation from China.
Pakistan’s restrictions reportedly went further than Beijing’s own rules, which permit some Taiwanese airline operations in mainland Chinese airspace.
China and Pakistan maintain close political and military ties, describing their relationship as an “all-weather strategic cooperative partnership.” China is Pakistan’s principal arms supplier, and Islamabad has consistently supported Beijing position on Taiwan.
Taiwanese airlines largely avoided Russian airspace after the escalation of the Ukraine conflict in 2022, although neither Moscow nor Taipei formally prohibited them from using it. Following the Pakistani restrictions, several Taiwan-Europe flights were rerouted through Russia.
According to Bloomberg, no country had previously imposed a blanket overflight ban on Taiwanese commercial airlines. In April, Seychelles, Mauritius, and Madagascar withdrew overflight clearances for Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te’s aircraft, forcing him to postpone a visit to Eswatini. Lai eventually made the trip in May.

WASHINGTON – US President Donald Trump intensified his attacks on Alaska Democrat Mary Peltola following a news report that her allies had secretly recruited candidates to join the state’s US Senate race in order to dilute support for Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan.
“I think Dan Sullivan – the fake Dan Sullivan – and Mary Peltola should be, number one, they should be taken off the ballot, and number two, they should be prosecuted,” Trump told reporters on Oct 28.
There’s no clear legal mechanism for the Democrat’s removal from the race and Trump did not provide direct evidence that her or her campaign advisers broke the law.
The New York Times reported on Oct 28 that Peltola’s team engaged in a broad attempt to peel votes from Sullivan by recruiting spoilers into the race.
So-called “ballot-stacking” manoeuvres are common in US politics and are generally thought to be legal.
In a social media post earlier on Oct 28, Trump called the effort “illegal” and said Peltola should “suffer the legal and political consequences for what she has done”, including her own exclusion from the race.
“In Alaska, I don’t think Mary Peltola, after perpetrating such a terrible scheme, should be allowed to run, because this is election fraud,” he said in a subsequent post.
Peltola’s campaign did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Trump’s post.
Both her campaign and the Senate Democrats’ campaign arm have denied involvement in the candidate recruitment effort.
The plan, dubbed the “ballot composition project”, resulted in the candidacy of retired teacher Dan J. Sullivan, the Times reported.
Peltola’s campaign said in a statement that it “has no involvement with either Sullivan campaign”.
The Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee said in a statement that it, too, “is not involved with Dan J. Sullivan”.
Trump’s critics have called his attacks an attempt to nullify an election that could decide control of the Senate.

At Trump’s request, the Department of Justice (DOJ) filed a lawsuit seeking to pre-emptively block the certification of Senate election results in Alaska if Senator Sullivan loses by a close margin, citing the risk of “voter confusion” with two individuals on the ballot having similar names.
The department argued that Daniel J. Sullivan is running as a deliberate spoiler to Senator Sullivan’s re-election campaign.
In a filing on Oct 28 in the federal court in Anchorage, the DOJ said that in the light of the New York Times report, the US intends to quickly seek information from Peltola’s campaign about whether it “attempted to deceive the court by seeking an expedited ruling on a motion to dismiss when the campaign may have been aware of the New York Times reporting before it was published”.
Trump last week said he was very concerned about the race, accusing Democrats of “election interference”. BLOOMBERG

In the letter, Flavio, son of former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro, alleged electoral fraud without providing evidence, accusing Brazil's Supreme Federal Court (STF) of overstepping the electoral court's authority.

The STF ordered voting to be extended until 7 p.m. on Sunday after both presidential campaigns reported difficulty voters faced in reaching polling stations. The ruling ultimately applied only to polling stations that had remained open at 5 p.m., while those already closed were not reopened.

Details

The EU offers Canada a different format for cooperation

At the same time, according to Politico, Brussels is not abandoning plans to significantly expand cooperation with Ottawa in the economic sphere, security issues, and strategic autonomy.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said that what matters to his country is not the formal names of future relations, but their practical results.
The good news is that specific names or terminology do not matter. What matters is how this will change the lives of Canadians
The updated text of the joint declaration was prepared on the eve of the EU-Canada summit in Montreal. At the time of Politico's publication, the document still required final approval.

How Bedouin voters became a defining story of Israel's 2026 election - analysis
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-28

08:03:32 KST

- i24NEWS

- How Bedouin voters became a defining story of Israel's 2026 election - analysis
How Bedouin voters became a defining story of Israel's 2026 election - analysis
No one’s told you, and no one will. But we have a winner coming out of Election Day: The Israeli political system
Yesterday in the middle of the Negev Desert, something amazing happened. Negev Bedouin, the poorest people in our country, came out in the some of the highest numbers. The credit belongs to them. And also to the system.
https://x.com/i/web/status/2115573810833289637
This post can't be displayed because social networks cookies have been deactivated. You can activate them by clicking .
Israel’s system brings the splinters of this country real representation. These groups don’t get diluted by district lines for electing lawmakers.
They don’t get stuffed by being thrown into giant political parties that have to have to big tent.
No. They can put up parties, run candidates, and play politics on their own. With the big boys.
It works. And it renews the Israeli system time after time.
We've seen it with the Shas Party, forged by discrimination by Ashkenazi ultra-Orthodox against Sephardic counterparts. With immigrants from the former Soviet Union, especially in their early years in the country. Groups continue to try it, understanding that at first they may not succeed.
That happened in this cycle with a tiny party representing ultra-Orthodox who want change in their community on education, work, and military service.
So, yes, we have a lot of parties, and we have a lot of elections, and we have a lot of chaos. But our destruction is creative destruction. Creating a country where politics matter, where politics move forward. And where, with fits and starts, politics really and truly can include everyone.
Marginalized groups come out in the Israeli system because they know they come out of the polling place with members of Knesset who represent them. They don’t need to fight inside some big-tent party. Or make do with a representative of a district with lines on a map.
No. A party, in this the Raam Party, that represents them.
Israel’s system excels at that and has done it time after time. The wider public doesn’t always like the results. Narrow constituencies can be frustrating.
People hate our system. They say it has too many parties. Too many elections. And too much chaos.
What happened yesterday should put those arguments in the waste basket. As 77% of Israelis went to cast their ballots.

US President Donald Trump has demanded that Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola and a rival sharing the name of Alaska's Republican incumbent be removed from next week's election ballot, accusing Democrats of an illegal scheme to confuse voters.
His call followed a New York Times investigation reporting that Democratic operatives had secretly recruited so-called "spoiler" candidates, including another Dan Sullivan, in an effort to draw votes away from Republican Senator Dan Sullivan.
"It has just been determined that the Democrats in Alaska illegally searched for, and recruited, a man named Dan Sullivan," Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform.
He alleged that Democrats had committed perjury by making false statements under oath in federal court, and demanded that the incumbent be allowed to run without either Peltola or the "FAKE Dan Sullivan" on the ballot.
And he told reporters later that Peltola and any other alleged accomplices should be prosecuted. "To me, that's voter fraud at the highest level," he said.
But the Times noted that recruiting candidates to split an opponent's vote, a practice known as ballot stacking, is generally legal and has been used by both parties.
As recently as 2024, little-known former Republican Anthony Frascone beat Democrat Mondaire Jones in a low-turnout Working Families Party primary in New York state.
Peltola 'definitely aware'
Among those it said were recruited was Daniel J. Sullivan, a retired teacher from a remote Alaskan fishing community. He has said he entered the race of his own volition.
The newspaper identified Democratic operative Jerid Kurtz as a central figure, reporting that he travelled around Alaska under an assumed name to court potential candidates.
Peltola's former campaign manager Elisa Rios told the paper the candidate was "definitely aware" of the project but not directly involved.
Peltola's campaign has denied recruiting any candidates.
The revelations come days after Trump ordered the Justice Department to sue Alaska over the second Sullivan's presence on the ballot.
The lawsuit seeks to delay certification if Peltola narrowly defeats the incumbent and votes cast for his namesake could have changed the outcome.
On Wednesday, US Vice President JD Vance defended the Trump administration’s legal challenge to Alaska’s Senate election, describing the candidacy of a second candidate with a name nearly identical to that of the incumbent as a “big fraud” and arguing that it could confuse voters ahead of next week’s midterm elections.
He argued that many voters would recognise the alleged problem but said others might be confused because of competing demands on their time.

Estonia to Build 150 Military Bunkers Near Russian Border for Baltic Defense Line
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-28
22:28:43 UTC
07:28:43 KST

- Category
- World
Estonia to Build 150 Military Bunkers Near Russian Border for Baltic Defense Line
Estonia’s Defense Minister, Martin Herem, revealed plans to construct roughly 150 military bunkers across the northeastern region of Ida-Viru County.
The construction forms part of the broader Baltic Defense Line initiative, according to ERR on October 28.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
Under the current layout, 100 of these structures are designated for state-owned territory, while around 50 will stand on municipal or privately held land.
Placing installations on private real estate requires formal agreements with property owners. Government officials are considering various options to resolve property usage, including financial compensation for inconveniences, land leasing, or outright purchasing of the needed parcels.
“But, according to my information, currently there are no large-scale plans for the state to acquire a wider belt,” Herem added.
Estonia’s bunker project aligns with broader regional efforts, following Finland's completion of a major fencing project along its own border with Russia.
Finland completed roughly 200 kilometers of new fencing along selected sections of its border with Russia as part of a broader effort to harden NATO’s eastern frontier. Launched in 2023, the project cost approximately $413 million and featured a tall metal mesh fence equipped with surveillance cameras, lighting, loudspeakers, and an adjacent patrol road for border guards.
Finnish authorities originally initiated the construction to prevent unauthorized crossings, but the initiative ultimately became part of a wider regional push among northern and eastern European nations to fortify their borders facing Russia and Belarus.

36 countries have officially confirmed their participation in Eurovision 2027, including Ukraine, while Canada will make its debut in the competition
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
00:23:48 EET
07:23:48 KST

36 countries have officially confirmed their participation in Eurovision 2027, including Ukraine, while Canada will make its debut in the competition
Kyiv • UNN
At least 36 countries will take part in Eurovision 2027 in Burgas, including Ukraine. Canada will make its debut, while North Macedonia will return.
Ukraine has joined the list of 36 countries that have officially confirmed their participation in the international song contest "Eurovision 2027." Next year, the contest will be held in the Bulgarian city of Burgas, and Canada will take part for the first time. This was reported by Lithuanian broadcaster LRT, citing the European Broadcasting Union (EBU), writes UNN.
Details
According to the organizers, the 71st Eurovision Song Contest will take place in May 2027. The semi-finals are scheduled for May 11 and 13, while the final will be held on May 15.
In addition to Ukraine, the United Kingdom, France, Germany, Italy, Poland, Sweden, Norway, Finland, Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia, and other countries have already confirmed their participation. At the same time, North Macedonia will return to the contest after a four-year hiatus.
The number of Eurovision participants may increase further
So far, broadcasters from 36 countries have confirmed their participation in the contest, but the final list may expand. In particular, Slovenia and Spain have not yet decided whether to participate. The European Broadcasting Union has given them until December to decide.
According to the preliminary plan, representatives of 31 countries will perform in the two semi-finals. Twenty performers will advance to the final, where they will be joined by representatives of the host country, Bulgaria, and four countries that automatically qualify for the final: France, Germany, Italy, and the United Kingdom.
In the semi-finals, the results will be determined by viewers, while in the final, both viewers and a professional jury will vote.
The allocation of countries between the semi-finals will be announced after the draw, scheduled to take place in Burgas in January 2027.
It will be recalled that the winner of Eurovision 2026 was Bulgarian representative Dara.

MOSCOW, Oct. 28 (Xinhua) -- Customs duties on goods imported into the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) have been fully eliminated for 32 African countries, Russian President Vladimir Putin said Wednesday.
Speaking at a meeting with representatives of major African regional organizations, Putin said exporters from 47 African countries benefit from tariff preferences when their goods enter EAEU markets.
"These benefits are available to 47 countries on the continent, and for 32 of them, customs duties have been completely eliminated," he said.
Formed in 2015, the EAEU groups Russia, Kazakhstan, Belarus, Kyrgyzstan and Armenia, aiming to modernize and enhance the competitiveness of their economies, strengthen cooperation and foster stable development to improve living standards in member states. ■

U.S. Fed holds interest rate steady ahead of midterm elections
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
05:26:08 CST
06:26:08 KST

U.S. Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh speaks at a press conference in Washington, D.C., the United States, Oct. 28, 2026. The U.S. Federal Reserve on Wednesday kept its target range for the federal funds rate unchanged at 3.75 to 4 percent, less than a week ahead of the 2026 midterm elections. (Photo by Li Yuanqing/Xinhua)
NEW YORK, Oct. 28 (Xinhua) -- The U.S. Federal Reserve on Wednesday kept its target range for the federal funds rate unchanged at 3.75 to 4 percent, less than a week ahead of the 2026 midterm elections.
"Economic activity is expanding at a strong pace. While uncertainty remains elevated owing, in part, to geopolitical developments, domestic spending has been resilient. Productivity growth is strong, and capital investment is robust. Job gains have kept pace with the workforce, and the unemployment rate has changed little," said the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) in a statement.
Nevertheless, inflation remains elevated. In support of the Federal Reserve's dual mandate, "the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3-3/4 to 4 percent," the FOMC said.
The committee reaffirmed "its policy of maintaining ample reserves in the banking system" and "price stability," saying the accumulation of more information will help the committee "determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the Committee's 2 percent goal."
Of the 12 FOMC members, 10 voted to keep the rate unchanged, while two favored a rate hike.
"Since our policy action in September, we have started to see some changes in financial and credit conditions. They have tightened for some businesses and households, much as we would expect," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said at a press conference after the FOMC meeting. "Market participants are becoming somewhat more discerning in their capital allocations."
Financial conditions broadly are helping create a path toward price stability. But with the near-term inflation picture still too high, "it's our responsibility to get inflation down," Warsh said, adding that the Fed's discussion over recent days "focused mainly on the price stability side of our remit."
Warsh announced that the Fed will change its meeting schedule in coming years. The FOMC will still meet eight times a year.
"But in 2027, one meeting will focus exclusively on broad monetary policy strategy, with neither a vote on the federal funds rate nor a policy statement anticipated," he said, adding that he expects there will be two strategy sessions in 2028.
The change in the meeting schedule will allow the Fed time to think about "big questions," Warsh said.
Responding to a question about U.S. President Donald Trump's assertion that other board members want to see the country "do badly," Warsh said he will not respond to quotes from public officials.
Following the Fed's decision to keep the rate unchanged, major U.S. stock indexes kept steady, while U.S. bond yields and the U.S. dollar index rose slightly.
The Fed's pause is within market expectations after its first rate hike in three years in September. Chris Hodge, chief U.S. economist at Natixis, said in a research note earlier in the week that pausing would allow more time to determine whether recent high inflation readings were part of a larger trend.
"Inflation is still the No. 1 problem in the U.S. economy, and there are a lot of signs it is getting more broad-based," Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union, told CNBC. However, "given that it's right before an election, they won't hike in October."
U.S. midterm elections fall on Nov. 3. To avoid impacting the power held by each political party, the Fed has mostly maintained its charted course in previous election cycles, except in 1978, 1982, 2018 and 2022, when inflation ran high.
The Federal Reserve's decision to hold rates steady at the October meeting suggests its prior hawkish stance was a matter of empty showmanship, Cem Karsan, founder and CIO at Kai Wealth, told CNBC. "At the end of the day, they're trying to gain credibility." Karsan said the only way to respond to what is important is through more dovishness from the Fed.
Nevertheless, it is widely expected that a hike in December is still in the cards. ■

World Bank approves 100-mln-USD loan for Uzbekistan's power grid modernization
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
05:26:04 CST
06:26:04 KST

TASHKENT, Oct. 28 (Xinhua) -- The World Bank Board of Executive Directors has approved a 100-million-U.S.-dollar loan to help Uzbekistan modernize its electricity distribution system, according to a bank statement.
The program will upgrade and digitalize 60 key substations nationwide to reduce energy losses, improve power supply reliability, and ease limits on integrating renewable energy into the grid.
By 2031, the program is expected to cut annual electricity losses at renovated substations by 20,000 megawatt-hours, enable the integration of at least 3.3 gigawatts (GW) of renewable energy, and avoid nearly 23,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent in emissions each year. It is also estimated to help create around 11,700 jobs within five years after the modernized facilities become operational.
The total budget for the program stands at 371 million dollars, which includes a 200-million-dollar loan approved by the Asian Development Bank on Sept. 30 and a 71-million-dollar contribution from Uzbekistan's state budget.
The project, implemented by the Joint-Stock Company National Electric Grid of Uzbekistan, supports the country's target to increase installed renewable energy capacity to 25 GW by 2030. ■

Intercommunal violence in southern Ethiopia displaces thousands: UN
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
05:26:03 CST
06:26:03 KST

UNITED NATIONS, Oct. 28 (Xinhua) -- UN humanitarians on Wednesday voiced deep concern about the intercommunal violence in the Ethiopian town of Moyale on the border with Kenya that has displaced thousands of people.
Casualties have been reported, along with disruptions to transport, markets and cross-border trade, limiting access to essential goods and services, said the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA).
On the Ethiopian side, the violence that erupted on Oct. 18 has reportedly displaced thousands of people in Oromia and Somali regions. This is in addition to the thousands of people who have reportedly crossed into Kenya, it said.
Local authorities in Kenya estimate that up to 50,000 people have crossed into the country since Thursday, amid reports of further crossings, it said.
Many of those fleeing are women and children. While some are staying with relatives and host communities, others have sought shelter in temporary locations, such as schools and churches. Food remains the most urgent need, alongside safe drinking water, emergency shelter, sanitation and health care, said the office.
"Continued insecurity has forced several partners to suspend activities," OCHA said. "The UN and its partners are preparing a joint assessment mission to areas affected by the violence as soon as security conditions permit."
It is critical to ensure the safety of the population, as well as safe, sustained and unimpeded humanitarian access to all people in need, said the office.
The UN Refugee Agency (UNHCR) has deployed an emergency team to Moyale and is working closely with the Kenyan government, UN agencies, the Kenya Red Cross Society and other humanitarian partners to support the national and local response, said OCHA.
The Kenya Red Cross Society is operating six health service points, screening for malnutrition and distributing relief items. Local communities have shared food and water, though their stocks are limited, said OCHA.
The UN and its humanitarian partners are working to scale up the response. UN agencies have deployed staff and are mobilizing additional supplies, including to prepare for potential further displacement. UNHCR is mobilizing emergency relief supplies, including essential household items and temporary shelter materials, to support nearly 12,000 people, with efforts under way to scale up assistance as needs grow, said OCHA. ■

Portugal to subsidize up to 80 pct of electric vehicle cost for low-income families
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
05:25:56 CST
06:25:56 KST

LISBON, Oct. 28 (Xinhua) -- Portugal's government announced Wednesday a new package of electric vehicle subsidies that includes, for the first time, a dedicated program for low-income households covering up to 80 percent of the purchase price, Environment Minister Maria da Graca Carvalho told parliament.
The program will support the acquisition of up to 20,000 vehicles for vulnerable families, with co-financing of up to 80 percent of the vehicle's value.
A parallel scheme for the general population, with rules similar to previous programs, will have a budget of approximately 50 million euros (56 million U.S. dollars).
The government will also support the purchase of up to 9,000 electric vehicles for micro-enterprises and will promote the acquisition of more sustainable heavy vehicles, alongside investment in their charging infrastructure.
Electric buses for low-density areas, to be used for worker and student mobility, will also be co-financed.
The previous electric vehicle subsidy program had a total budget of 10 million euros (11.2 million dollars), with incentives of up to 4,000 euros (4,480 dollars) for new fully electric vehicles priced up to 38,500 euros (43,120 dollars), or up to 55,000 euros (61,600 dollars) for models with more than five seats.
Carvalho framed the announcement in the context of Portugal's ongoing energy crisis, saying that "freeing Portugal from dependence on fossil fuels is not a chimera: it is an essential condition for a better future and less dependence on third parties." ■

News Analysis: Britain's budget targets breathing space for households, businesses
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-29
05:25:54 CST
06:25:54 KST

LONDON, Oct. 28 (Xinhua) -- British Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey on Wednesday unveiled the Budget 2026, aiming to give families and firms breathing space from rising costs through supporting measures in the fields including energy, income, housing, spending and business tax.
The government will provide 100 pounds (about 133 U.S. dollars) household energy payment for up to 20 million qualified households in England, with funding for similar support provided to the rest of the UK. Meanwhile, it will extend the value-added-tax cut on electricity bills to July 1, 2027, according to the budget.
The budget supports drivers by extending the cut to fuel duty for a further six months, while cutting prices at local, lower-powered public chargers to reduce costs for electric vehicle drivers who rely on them.
Earlier Wednesday, the Chancellor also abolished standing charges on household gas bills, a fixed daily fee added on top of a household gas bill regardless of how much gas has been used.
In response to the rising inflation, the government will remove tariffs from more than 100 products to lower import costs for everyday family spending such as baked beans and chocolate, and cut tariffs on kerosene and fertilizer to support households and farmers facing higher costs.
At the same time, the budget plans to increase the National Living Wage by 3.9 percent per hour on April 1, 2027.
Moreover, the budget provides a further 1.5 billion pounds (about 2 billion dollars) in funding for social and affordable housing, taking total capital investment over the next 10 years above 40 billion pounds (about 53 billion dollars).
On the front of business support, the budget backs England's high streets with a package that means all retail, hospitality and leisure properties in England will see their business rates either frozen in real terms, reduced or cut to zero.
On top of the extra 20 percent business rates cut for pubs and all but the largest live music venues, announced in July, this package will take around 70,000 more retail, hospitality and leisure businesses out of business rates by increasing the Small Business Rates Relief threshold.
To deal with the energy price hikes faced by enterprises, measures will be taken to support over 10,000 eligible businesses in electricity intensive Industrial Strategy sectors and the foundational sectors in their supply chains to cut electricity bills by up to 25 percent and bring electricity costs closer to other economies in Europe from April 2027.
However, due to the limited momentum of change brought by the budget, analysts believe there should be more ambitious plans from the government to increase living standard and boost business investment in the country.
"For this budget, the outcome for UK residents is really one in which Healey tinkers around the edges," John Bryson, a professor at the University of Birmingham, told Xinhua.
Since forecasts anticipate energy bills will rise again by as much as 27 percent in January, the government also needs to be thinking more long-term about how to protect households from rising energy bills not just in the short term but over a sustained period, said Caitlin Robinson, a professor at the University of Bristol.
This will require more ambitious investment in energy efficiency, low carbon heating and renewable electricity, Robinson added.
"This was a 'steady as you go' budget, sending the right signals to business, but lacking big calls that would really shift the economic dial," Shevaun Haviland, director general of the British Chambers of Commerce, said.
"Our key tests for the Chancellor were whether his plans would boost growth and ease costs for business. Many firms will have been hoping for a greater impact," she noted.
Tina McKenzie, national chair of the Federation of Small Businesses, hoped the increase in Small Business Rates Relief should have covered more businesses, such as manufacturers, small exporters, nurseries and office-based businesses which are not just on the high streets.
Eamonn O'Brien, chair of the Local Government Association, argued that no overall funding increase for local government means councils will continue to struggle to meet demand and provide services to their communities. ■

America's largest budget airline reports 71% jump in airfare
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-28
20:06:19 UTC
05:06:19 KST

Frontier Airlines reported a 71% increase in airfare in the third quarter as the country's largest budget airline tried to pass along an even bigger jump in jet fuel prices.
Frontier's fare revenue averaged $67.82 per passenger in the third quarter, compared with $39.74 last year. Including the budget airline's many fees, such as for checked and carry-on luggage, total revenue per passenger rose 30% on the year to $138.22.
Customers kept booking despite the higher prices. Frontier's passenger count rose 18% to more than 9.8 million people in the quarter. That's a difference of 1.5 million passengers from last year.
The company said demand remains strong, even at these higher prices, but Frontier still lost money as it took a $134 million charge tied to the return of some Airbus aircraft. Excluding that and other one-time charges, Frontier had an adjusted profit of $40 million.
Its posted a net loss of $104 million compared with a $77 million loss a year earlier. Its fuel bill soared 82% to $425 million.
Frontier forecast potential adjusted profit in the fourth quarter, saying it expects to post an adjusted loss of 15 cents per share to adjusted earnings of as much as 5 cents per share.
Carriers from Delta Air Lines to Frontier have said customers are mostly continuing to book flights despite higher fares, but that record jet fuel prices, their biggest cost after labor, are eroding profits.
Frontier shares rose close to 12%.
Frontier had eclipsed Spirit Airlines as the biggest discount carrier in the country even before that airline collapsed in May.
